sentences.zh: 周浚

translations.literal: Zhou Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun

sentences.zh: 周浚，字開林，汝南安成人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Jun, courtesy name Kailin, was a man of Ancheng in Runan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Jun, whose courtesy name was Kailin, came from Ancheng in Runan.

sentences.zh: 父裴，少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Pei was Director of the Palace Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Pei, had served as Director of the Palace Treasury.

sentences.zh: 浚性果烈。

translations.literal: Jun by nature was decisive and fierce.
translations.idiomatic: He was by nature resolute and uncompromising.

sentences.zh: 以才理見知，有人倫鑒識。

translations.literal: By talent and reasoning he was recognized; he had insight for judging people.
translations.idiomatic: His talent and clarity of mind won him recognition, and he had a keen eye for character.

sentences.zh: 鄉人史曜素微賤，眾所未知，浚獨引之為友，遂以妹妻之，曜竟有名於世。

translations.literal: His fellow townsman Shi Yao had always been lowly and base; the crowd did not know him, but Jun alone took him as friend, then gave him his younger sister in marriage, and Yao in the end had a name in the world.
translations.idiomatic: A townsman, Shi Yao, had long been poor and obscure, and everyone else overlooked him, but Jun alone befriended him, married his sister to him, and Yao eventually made a name for himself in the world.

sentences.zh: 浚初不應州郡之辟，後仕魏為尚書郎。

translations.literal: At first Jun did not respond to summons from the province or commandery; later he served Wei as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He at first refused appointments from provincial and commandery authorities, then entered Wei service as a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 累遷御史中丞，拜折沖將軍、揚州刺史，封射陽侯。

translations.literal: By successive promotions he reached Palace Assistant Secretary, was appointed General Who Subdues the Foe and Inspector of Yang province, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Sheyang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Palace Assistant Secretary, was named General Who Subdues the Foe and Inspector of Yang province, and enfeoffed as Marquis of Sheyang.

sentences.zh: 隨王渾伐吳，攻破江西屯戍，與孫皓中軍大戰，斬偽丞相張悌等首級數千，俘馘萬計，進軍屯于橫江。

translations.literal: He followed Wang Hun in the campaign against Wu, broke the garrison posts on the west of the river, fought a great battle with Sun Hao's central army, beheaded several thousand including the false Chancellor Zhang Ti and others, took prisoners and severed heads by the tens of thousands, and advanced the army to camp at Hengjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned with Wang Hun against Wu, stormed the Jiangxi garrisons, and clashed with Sun Hao's main force, taking several thousand heads including those of the puppet chancellor Zhang Ti and others and tens of thousands of captives, then pushed forward and encamped at Hengjiang.

sentences.zh: 時聞龍驤將軍王濬既破上方，別駕何惲說浚曰：「張悌率精銳之卒，悉吳國之眾，殄滅于此，吳之朝野莫不震懾。

translations.literal: At the time it was heard that General Who Spreads Might Wang Jun had already broken the upper sector, and Assistant Officer He Yun persuaded Jun, saying: "Zhang Ti led crack troops and the full host of Wu; they were exterminated here, and none in Wu's court or countryside was not awestruck.
translations.idiomatic: Word arrived that General Who Spreads Might Wang Jun had already broken the upper defenses, and He Yun, the assistant officer, urged Jun: "Zhang Ti committed Wu's best troops and virtually its entire army here, and they were wiped out; the whole of Wu is shaken."

sentences.zh: 今王龍驤既破武昌，兵威甚盛，順流而下，所向輒克，土崩之勢見矣。

translations.literal: Now Wang Longxiang has already taken Wuchang; his military might is very great; going downstream wherever he turns he prevails; the situation of earth crumbling is visible.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun has now seized Wuchang, his army is formidable, and sweeping downriver he wins every fight; the collapse of Wu is plain to see.

sentences.zh: 竊謂宜速渡江，直指建鄴，大軍卒至，奪其膽氣，可不戰而擒。

translations.literal: I privately say it is fitting to cross the river speedily, point straight at Jianye, the great army arriving suddenly, seize their courage and spirit, and then without battle capture them.
translations.idiomatic: I believe we should cross the Yangzi at once, drive straight on Jianye, and hit the capital before they recover their nerve so we can take them without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 」浚善其謀，便使白渾。

translations.literal: Jun approved his plan and then sent someone to report to Hun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun approved the plan and had the proposal put to Wang Hun.

sentences.zh: 惲曰：「渾暗於事機，而欲慎己免咎，必不我從。

translations.literal: Yun said: Hun is dim about the turning points of affairs and wishes to be cautious for himself and avoid blame; he certainly will not follow me.
translations.idiomatic: He Yun replied that Wang Hun was blind to the moment and only wanted to shield himself from blame, and that he would not listen to them.

sentences.zh: 」浚固使白之，渾果曰：「受詔但令江北抗衡吳軍，不使輕進。

translations.literal: Jun firmly sent to report it to him, and Hun indeed said: I received edicts that only ordered me to oppose Wu's army north of the river and did not allow rash advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jun insisted on passing it up, and Hun answered as expected that his orders were only to hold Wu north of the river, not to advance recklessly.

sentences.zh: 貴州雖武，豈能獨平江東！

translations.literal: Though your province is martial, how can it alone pacify Jiangdong!
translations.idiomatic: Your command may be strong, but it cannot by itself subdue everything east of the river!

sentences.zh: 今者違命，勝不足多；

translations.literal: Now if we disobey the order, victory is not worth much;
translations.idiomatic: If we defy those orders now, even victory would count for little;

sentences.zh: 若其不勝，為罪已重。

translations.literal: if we do not win, the guilt is already heavy.
translations.idiomatic: if we lose, the fault will be crushing.

sentences.zh: 且詔令龍驤受我節度，但當具君舟楫，一時俱濟耳。

translations.literal: Moreover the edict ordered Longxiang to accept my command; you need only prepare your boats and oars and cross together at one time.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the edict puts Wang Jun under my command; you have only to ready your flotilla and we can all cross together.

sentences.zh: 」惲曰：「龍驤克萬里之寇，以既濟之功來受節度，未之聞也。

translations.literal: Yun said: That Longxiang, having conquered a foe ten thousand li away, should then, with merit already achieved, come accept command—this I have not heard of.
translations.idiomatic: Yun objected that he had never heard of a general who had crushed an enemy a thousand miles away and already crossed the river being told to take orders after the fact.

sentences.zh: 且握兵之要，可則奪之，所謂受命不受辭也。

translations.literal: Moreover the essential of holding troops: when it is possible, seize it—this is what is called receiving a charge without accepting wording.
translations.idiomatic: The heart of command is to seize the opportunity when you can—that is accepting a mandate without letting wording tie your hands.

sentences.zh: 今渡江必全克獲，將有何慮？

translations.literal: Now if we cross the river we are sure to achieve full capture; what worry will there be?
translations.idiomatic: A crossing now would complete the victory; what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 若疑於不濟，不可謂智；

translations.literal: If one doubts that it will not succeed, that cannot be called wisdom;
translations.idiomatic: To doubt success is not wisdom;

sentences.zh: 知而不行，不可謂忠，實鄙州上下所以恨恨也。

translations.literal: to know and not act cannot be called loyalty; truly this is why high and low in our mean province are resentful.
translations.idiomatic: to see the right course and refuse it is not loyalty—and that is exactly why everyone in this command seethes with frustration.

sentences.zh: 」渾執不聽。

translations.literal: Hun held to his view and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Hun would not budge.

sentences.zh: 居無何而濬至，渾召之不來，乃直指三山，孫皓遂降於浚。

translations.literal: Before long Wang Jun arrived; Hun summoned him and he did not come, then went straight to Sanshan, and Sun Hao thereupon surrendered to Zhou Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wang Jun arrived, ignored Wang Hun's summons, and drove on to Mount San, where Sun Hao surrendered into Jin hands.

sentences.zh: 渾深恨之，而欲與浚爭功。

translations.literal: Hun deeply resented it and wished to contend merit with Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Hun bitterly resented him and tried to wrest the credit.

sentences.zh: 惲箋與浚曰：「《書》貴克讓，《易》大謙光，斯古文所詠，道家所崇。

translations.literal: Yun wrote a note to Jun, saying: "The Documents esteems being able to yield; the Changes magnifies the modesty's light; these are what old texts praise and what the Way esteems.
translations.idiomatic: He Yun wrote to Jun: "The Classic of Documents honors deference, the Changes praises the light of modesty—values the old texts celebrate and every thoughtful man respects.

sentences.zh: 前破張悌，吳人失氣，龍驤因之，陷其區宇。

translations.literal: Earlier we broke Zhang Ti; Wu's people lost their breath; Longxiang took advantage and penetrated their territory.
translations.idiomatic: We broke Zhang Ti and broke Wu's morale; Wang Jun rode that success into their heartland.

sentences.zh: 論其前後，我實緩師，動則為傷，事則不及。

translations.literal: Judging front and back, we truly slowed the army; if we move then there is harm; in the affair we did not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: Measured from start to finish, our wing really held the army back: any move on our part would have been risky, and we missed the decisive stroke.

sentences.zh: 而今方競其功。

translations.literal: Yet now he is contending for that merit.
translations.idiomatic: Yet now he is scrambling for the glory.

sentences.zh: 彼既不吞聲，將虧雍穆之弘，興矜爭之鄙，斯愚情之所不取也。

translations.literal: If he will not swallow his voice, he will harm the breadth of harmony and raise the baseness of boastful quarrel; this is what my foolish feeling does not approve.
translations.idiomatic: If he will not keep silent, he will spoil the larger harmony and stir up petty boasting—something I cannot in good conscience endorse.

sentences.zh: 」浚得箋，即諫止渾，渾不能納，遂相表奏。

translations.literal: " Jun received the note, immediately remonstrated to stop Hun; Hun could not accept it, and so they exchanged memorials to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Jun took the letter and urged Hun to relent, but Hun refused, and the two sides bombarded the court with competing memorials.

sentences.zh: 浚既濟江，與渾共行吳城壘，綏撫新附，以功進封成武侯，食邑六千戶，賜絹六千匹。

translations.literal: After Jun had crossed the river, together with Hun he inspected Wu's ramparts, comforted and soothed the newly attached, and by merit was advanced to enfeoffment as Marquis of Chengwu with six thousand households' fief and six thousand bolts of silk conferred.
translations.idiomatic: Once Zhou Jun had crossed the Yangzi, he toured Wu's fortifications with Wang Hun, pacified the newly submitted population, and for his service was promoted to Marquis of Chengwu with six thousand households and a gift of six thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 明年，移鎮秣陵。

translations.literal: The next year he shifted garrison to Moling.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he moved his headquarters to Moling.

sentences.zh: 時吳初平，屢有逃亡者，頻討平之。

translations.literal: At the time Wu had just been pacified; there were repeatedly those who fled; he frequently attacked and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu had only just been conquered, and desertions flared repeatedly; he put each outbreak down in turn.

sentences.zh: 賓禮故老，搜求俊乂，甚有威德，吳人悅服。

translations.literal: He guest-treated the old elders, searched and sought the outstandingly talented; he had very great awe-inspiring virtue, and Wu's people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He honored local elders, sought out able men, carried real moral authority, and won the Wu gentry's willing allegiance.

sentences.zh: 初，吳之未平也，浚在弋陽，南北為互市，而諸將多相襲奪以為功。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wu had not yet been pacified, Jun was at Yiyang; north and south had mutual markets, but the various generals mostly raided one another to seize credit.
translations.idiomatic: Before Wu fell, while Jun was stationed at Yiyang, Jin and Wu still traded across the border, yet many generals staged raids on those markets to pad their battle records.

sentences.zh: 吳將蔡敏守於沔中，其兄珪為將在秣陵，與敏書曰：「古者兵交，使在其間，軍國固當舉信義以相高。

translations.literal: Wu general Cai Min was guarding in the Han river region; his elder brother Gui was a general at Moling, and wrote to Min, saying: "In antiquity when arms crossed, envoys went between them; army and state ought indeed to raise faith and righteousness to honor one another.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu general Cai Min held a post along the Han while his brother Gui served at Moling; Gui wrote to him: "Even when armies face each other, diplomats still pass between them, and both sides are expected to show good faith.

sentences.zh: 而聞疆場之上，往往有襲奪互市，甚不可行，弟慎無為小利而忘大備也。

translations.literal: Yet I hear that on the borders often there is raiding and seizing of the mutual markets—very impermissible; younger brother, be careful not to for small gain forget great preparedness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I hear our frontier is full of raids on the border markets—that cannot stand. Brother, do not chase petty profit and forget the larger defense.

sentences.zh: 」候者得珪書以呈浚，浚曰：「君子也。

translations.literal: A scout obtained Gui's letter and presented it to Jun; Jun said: This is a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Patrols intercepted Gui's letter and brought it to Jun, who said, "Here is a true gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」及渡江，求珪，得之，問其本，曰；

translations.literal: When he crossed the river he sought Gui, obtained him, asked his origin, and he said:
translations.idiomatic: After crossing the river he searched out Gui, found him, and asked where he came from; Gui replied—

sentences.zh: 「汝南人也。

translations.literal: "I am a man of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: "I am from Runan.

sentences.zh: 」浚戲之曰：「吾固疑吳無君子，而卿果吾鄉人。」

translations.literal: Jun jested with him, saying: I had indeed doubted Wu had no gentleman, yet you truly are my fellow townsman.
translations.idiomatic: Jun teased him: "I used to think Wu had no gentlemen left; now I see one of my own countrymen after all."

sentences.zh: 遷侍中。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 武帝問浚：「卿宗後生，稱誰為可？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu asked Jun: "Among the younger men of your lineage, whom do you praise as capable?
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu asked him which younger members of the Zhou clan he rated most highly.

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「臣叔父子恢，稱重臣宗；

translations.literal: " He answered, saying: "My uncle's son Hui is praised as weighty in my lineage;
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "My cousin Hui, son of my uncle, is regarded as the solid pillar of the family;

sentences.zh: 從父子馥，稱清臣宗。

translations.literal: the son of my father's cousin Fu is praised as pure in my lineage.
translations.idiomatic: and my kinsman Fu, known for integrity, is the one they call the family's man of clear character.

sentences.zh: 」帝並召用。

translations.literal: " The Emperor summoned and employed both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned both men and gave them posts.

sentences.zh: 浚轉少府，以本官領將作大匠。

translations.literal: Jun was transferred to Director of the Palace Treasury, and in his original office concurrently supervised the Court Architect.
translations.idiomatic: Jun moved to Director of the Palace Treasury while continuing as Court Architect.

sentences.zh: 改營宗廟訖，增邑五百戶。

translations.literal: When the rebuilding of the imperial ancestral temple was finished, his fief was increased by five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial temple project was complete, his fief was enlarged by five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後代王渾為使持節、都督揚州諸軍事、安東將軍，卒于位。

translations.literal: Later he replaced Wang Hun as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs of Yang province, and General Who Guards the East, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He later succeeded Wang Hun as military governor of Yang province and General Who Guards the East, holding the credential staff, and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 三子：顗、嵩、謨。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Yi, Song, and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Zhou Yi, Zhou Song, and Zhou Mo.

sentences.zh: 顗嗣爵，別有傳云。

translations.literal: Yi inherited the title; elsewhere there is a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi inherited the title and has his own biography elsewhere.

translations.literal: The transmitted text shows a lone '=' sign as a layout marker between sub-biographies.
translations.idiomatic: (Subsection divider in the received text.)

sentences.zh: 子嵩

translations.literal: The son Song.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Song

sentences.zh: =嵩字仲智，狷直果俠，每以才氣陵物。

translations.literal: Song, courtesy name Zhongzhi, was narrow, upright, decisive, and chivalrous; he constantly by talent and spirit looked down on things.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Song, courtesy name Zhongzhi, was rigid, blunt, bold, and chivalrous, and habitually rode roughshod over others with his talent and swagger.

sentences.zh: 元帝作相，引為參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Langya was Chancellor, he brought him in as an Army Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: While still serving as grand counselor, the future Yuan-di appointed him an army adviser.

sentences.zh: 及帝為晉王，又拜奉朝請。

translations.literal: When the Emperor became Prince of Jin, he again was appointed Courtier for Palace Appearances.
translations.idiomatic: When his patron was invested as Prince of Jin, Song was named a courtier for palace appearances.

sentences.zh: 嵩上疏曰：「臣聞取天下者，常以無事。

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that those who take the empire always use non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Song presented a memorial: "I have read that those who win the realm do so in times of calm.

sentences.zh: 及其有事，不足以取天下。

translations.literal: When they have affairs, it is not sufficient to take the empire.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis drives policy, that is no longer enough to win the realm.

sentences.zh: 故古之王者，必應天順時，義全而後取，讓成而後得，是以享世長久，重光萬載也。

translations.literal: Therefore the kings of antiquity necessarily responded to Heaven and followed the times; righteousness was complete and afterward they took; yielding was accomplished and afterward they obtained; by this they enjoyed generations long-lasting, doubled brightness ten thousand ages.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings answered Heaven and the season: they took power only when justice was complete and yielded only when deference was real, which is why their lines lasted and their virtue shone for ages.

sentences.zh: 今議者以殿下化流江漢，澤被六州，功濟蒼生，欲推崇尊號。

translations.literal: Now the discussers, because Your Highness's transforming influence flows through Jiang and Han and grace covers six provinces and merit aids the black-haired people, wish to promote and honor exalted titles.
translations.idiomatic: Now some argue that because Your Highness's influence spreads through the Jiang and Han heartland, your bounty reaches six provinces, and you have saved the common people, the time has come to press an exalted title on you.

sentences.zh: 臣謂今梓宮未反，舊京未清，義夫泣血，士女震動；

translations.literal: Your subject says: now the spirit coffin has not returned, the old capital is not cleared, righteous men weep blood, gentlemen and ladies tremble;
translations.idiomatic: I say the late emperor's catafalque has not returned, the old capital is still in enemy hands, loyal men weep blood, and the realm is shaken;

sentences.zh: 宜深明周公之道，先雪社稷大恥，盡忠言嘉謀之助，以時濟弘仁之功，崇謙謙之美，推後己之誠；

translations.literal: it is fitting deeply to clarify the way of the Duke of Zhou, first to wash away the great shame of the altars of soil and grain, exhaust loyal words and fine plans' aid, in season to complete the work of vast benevolence, honor the beauty of modest modesty, push the sincerity of putting self behind;
translations.idiomatic: you should follow the Duke of Zhou's example, avenge the state's deepest humiliation first, heed loyal counsel, in due course complete the work of restoring benevolent rule, prize modest deference, and show you put the realm ahead of private ambition;

sentences.zh: 然後揖讓以謝天下，誰敢不應，誰敢不從！

translations.literal: afterward bow and yield to thank the empire—who dares not respond, who dares not follow!
translations.idiomatic: only then yield the throne in ritual gratitude to the world—who then would dare refuse you, who would dare not follow!

sentences.zh: 」由是忤旨，出為新安太守。

translations.literal: " By this he disobeyed the intent and went out as Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: The advice offended the throne, and he was sent out as administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 嵩怏怏不悅，臨發，與散騎郎張嶷在侍中戴邈坐，褒貶朝士，又詆毀邈，邈密表之。

translations.literal: Song was displeased and unhappy; as he was about to depart, together with Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry Zhang Yi he sat in Palace Attendant Dai Miao's presence, praised and blamed court gentlemen, and also slandered Miao; Miao secretly memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: Sullen at the demotion, on the eve of departure he sat with the gentleman of scattered cavalry Zhang Yi in Palace Attendant Dai Miao's quarters, passed judgment on court figures, and abused Miao as well; Miao slipped a secret memorial to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝召嵩入，面責之曰：「卿矜豪傲慢，敢輕忽朝廷，由吾不德故耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Song in and face-to-face rebuked him, saying: "You are arrogant and proud and dare to slight the court; it is because I lack virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called him in and rebuked him to his face: "You swagger and despise the court because you think me without virtue.

sentences.zh: 」嵩跪謝曰：「昔唐虞至聖，四凶在朝。

translations.literal: " Song knelt and apologized, saying: "In the past Tang and Yu were utmost sage, yet the Four Fiends were at court.
translations.idiomatic: Song knelt and shot back: "Even under the sage-kings Yao and Shun, the Four Fiends still sat in council.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖聖明禦世，亦安能無碌碌之臣乎！

translations.literal: Although Your Majesty is sagely bright and governs the age, how can you be without mediocre ministers!
translations.idiomatic: A sage on the throne may still be stuck with mediocre men in his service!

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，收付廷尉。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was angry, seized him and handed him to the Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the emperor had him arrested and sent to the Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 廷尉華恆以嵩大不敬棄市論，嶷以扇和減罪除名。

translations.literal: Commandant Hua Heng judged Song for great irreverence with the penalty of execution in the market; Yi for fanning harmony had crime reduced and name removed.
translations.idiomatic: Commandant Hua Heng urged execution in the marketplace for gross lèse-majesté; Zhang Yi won a reduced sentence for trying to calm the dispute and was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 時顗方貴重，帝隱忍。

translations.literal: At the time Yi was just honored and weighty; the Emperor secretly endured.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhou Yi was then powerful at court, the emperor swallowed his anger for the moment.

sentences.zh: 久之，補廬陵太守，不之職，更拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed Administrator of Luling, did not go to office, and was again appointed Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was named administrator of Luling but never took up the post, and was instead made Palace Assistant Secretary.

sentences.zh: 是時帝以王敦勢盛，漸疏忌王導等。

translations.literal: At this time the Emperor because Wang Dun's power was flourishing gradually grew distant and jealous of Wang Dao and others.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wang Dun's power had grown so great that the emperor began to distance himself from Wang Dao and his circle.

sentences.zh: 嵩上疏曰：

translations.literal: Song submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Song drafted another memorial—

sentences.zh: 疏奏，帝感悟，故導等獲全。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, the Emperor was moved to insight, therefore Dao and the others obtained preservation.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached the throne, the emperor took the point, and Wang Dao and his allies were spared.

sentences.zh: 王敦既害顗而使人吊嵩，嵩曰：「亡兄天下人，為天下人所殺，復何所吊！

translations.literal: After Wang Dun had harmed Yi he sent someone to condole Song; Song said: "The lost elder brother was a man of the empire; killed by men of the empire—what further is there to condole!
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun murdered Zhou Yi he sent messengers to console Song, who retorted: "My brother belonged to the realm; the realm killed him—what is left to condole?

sentences.zh: 」敦甚銜之，懼失人情，故未加害，用為從事中郎。

translations.literal: " Dun deeply harbored resentment against him, feared losing human sentiment, therefore did not add harm, and employed him as Staff Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Dun nursed a deep grudge but dared not kill him for fear of popular backlash, so he named Song a staff supervisor instead.

sentences.zh: 嵩，王應嫂父也，以顗橫遇禍，意恆憤憤，嘗眾中云：「應不宜統兵。

translations.literal: Song was Wang Ying's uncle by marriage; because Yi met disaster across-wise, his intent was constantly resentful; he once in a crowd said: "Ying ought not command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Song was Wang Ying's uncle by marriage; Zhou Yi's murder left him simmering, and he once declared in public that Wang Ying was unfit to hold military command.

sentences.zh: 」敦密使妖人李脫誣嵩及周筵潛相署置，遂害之。

translations.literal: " Dun secretly sent the sorcerer Li Tuo to falsely accuse Song and Zhou Yan of secretly appointing one another, and then harmed them.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then had the charlatan Li Tuo fabricate charges that Song and Zhou Yan were plotting clandestine appointments, and had Song killed on that pretext.

sentences.zh: 嵩精於事佛，臨刑猶於市誦經云。

translations.literal: Song was refined in serving the Buddha; facing execution he still in the market recited sutras, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Song was a devout Buddhist; even on the execution ground he was said to be chanting scripture.

sentences.zh: 子謨

translations.literal: The son Mo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhou Mo

sentences.zh: =謨以顗故，頻居顯職。

translations.literal: Mo because of Yi's reason repeatedly occupied illustrious posts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Mo, owing to Zhou Yi's standing, repeatedly rose to prominent offices.

sentences.zh: 王敦死後，詔贈戴若思、譙王承等，而未及顗。

translations.literal: After Wang Dun died, an edict posthumously honored Dai Ruosi, Prince Qiao Cheng, and others, but did not reach Yi.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Dun's death the court posthumously ennobled Dai Ruosi, Prince Cheng of Qiao, and others, yet still omitted Zhou Yi.

sentences.zh: 時謨為後軍將軍，上疏曰：

translations.literal: At the time Mo was Rear Army General and submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mo was then Rear Army General and submitted a memorial—

sentences.zh: 疏奏，不報。

translations.literal: When the memorial was presented, there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The throne never answered.

sentences.zh: 謨復重表，然後追贈顗官。

translations.literal: Mo again repeated the memorial; afterward posthumously Yi was ennobled with office.
translations.idiomatic: Mo pressed the issue with a second memorial, and only then did the court posthumously restore Zhou Yi's honors.

sentences.zh: 謨曆少府、丹陽尹、侍中、中護軍，封西平侯。

translations.literal: Mo passed through Director of the Palace Treasury, Administrator of Danyang, Palace Attendant, and General Who Guards the Army, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: Mo served as Director of the Palace Treasury, administrator of Danyang, palace attendant, and General Who Guards the Army, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 卒贈金紫光祿大夫，諡曰貞。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously awarded Grand Master of Golden Purple Gleam, posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court awarded him the posthumous title of grand master of golden purple gleam and the posthumous epithet "Loyal" (Zhen).

sentences.zh: 從父弟馥

translations.literal: Paternal cousin Fu.
translations.idiomatic: His paternal cousin Zhou Fu

sentences.zh: =馥字祖宣，浚從父弟也。

translations.literal: Fu, courtesy name Zuxuan, was Jun's paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, courtesy name Zuxuan, was Zhou Jun's paternal cousin.

sentences.zh: 父蕤，安平太守。

translations.literal: His father Rui was Administrator of Anping.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Zhou Rui, had been administrator of Anping.

sentences.zh: 馥少與友人成公簡齊名，俱起家為諸王文學，累遷司徒左西屬。

translations.literal: In youth Fu with his friend Cheng Gongjian had equal name; both rose from family to be literary scholars to the princes, and by successive promotions reached Western Subordinate of the Left under the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had been as celebrated as his friend Cheng Gongjian; both began as tutors to imperial princes and rose to serve as senior clerk on the minister of education's western staff.

sentences.zh: 司徒王渾表「馥理識清正，兼有才幹，主定九品，檢括精詳。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Wang Hun memorialized: "Fu's principles and insight are pure and upright, and moreover he has talent and capacity; presiding over fixing the nine ranks, his inspection and compilation are precise and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wang Hun reported that Fu's judgment was upright, that he combined talent with administrative skill, and that as chief arbiter of the nine-rank system his vetting had been meticulous.

sentences.zh: 臣委任責成，褒貶允當，請補尚書郎」。

translations.literal: Your subject delegated responsibility and demanded results; praise and blame were fittingly appropriate; I request to appoint him Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Hun added that he had delegated real authority to Fu, that Fu's praise and blame of candidates had been fair, and asked the court to appoint Fu gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 稍遷司徒左長史、吏部郎，選舉精密，論望益美。

translations.literal: By gradual promotion he reached Chief Clerk of the Left under the Minister of Education and Gentleman of the Personnel Bureau; selections and appointments were precise and close, and discussion of his reputation grew ever finer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to chief clerk on the minister of education's left and gentleman of the personnel bureau, where his appointments were meticulous and his reputation steadily improved.

sentences.zh: 轉御史中丞、侍中，拜徐州刺史，加冠軍將軍、假節。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Palace Assistant Secretary and Palace Attendant, appointed Inspector of Xu province, and additionally titled General Who Crowns the Army with credential staff.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Palace Assistant Secretary and palace attendant, became inspector of Xu province, and was given the extra titles of General Who Crowns the Army and credential staff.

sentences.zh: 徵為廷尉。

translations.literal: He was summoned to be Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned him to serve as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 惠帝幸鄴，成都王穎以馥守河南尹。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went to Ye, the Prince of Chengdu, Ying, put Fu in charge as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Hui was at Ye, Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, named Fu acting intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 陳眕、上官已等奉清河王覃為太子，加馥衛將軍、錄尚書，馥辭不受。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen, Shangguan Yi, and others set up the Prince of Qinghe, Tan, as heir apparent, added Fu as General Who Guards the Army and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, but Fu declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen and Shangguan Yi raised Sima Tan, Prince of Qinghe, as crown prince and offered Fu the posts of General Who Guards the Army and supervisor of the Masters of Writing; Fu refused them.

sentences.zh: 覃令馥與上官已合軍，馥認已小人縱暴，終為國賊，乃共司隸滿奮等謀共除之，謀泄，為已所襲，奮被害，馥走得免。

translations.literal: Tan ordered Fu to join armies with Shangguan Yi; Fu deemed Yi a petty man indulging in violence, in the end a traitor to the state, and therefore together with Metropolitan Commandant Man Fen and others plotted jointly to remove him; the plot leaked; he was raided by Yi; Fen was killed; Fu fled and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Tan told Fu to merge his troops with Shangguan Yi's, but Fu judged Yi a vicious upstart who would become a scourge to the realm, so he conspired with Metropolitan Commandant Man Fen and others to eliminate him. The plot leaked, Yi struck first, Man Fen was killed, and Fu barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 及已為張方所敗，召馥還攝河南尹。

translations.literal: When Yi was defeated by Zhang Fang, Fu was summoned back to act as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi was routed by Zhang Fang, Fu was recalled to resume duty as intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 暨東海王越迎大駕，以馥為中領軍，未就，遷司隸校尉，加散騎常侍、假節，都督諸軍事于澠池。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Donghai, Yue, welcomed the Grand Carriage, Fu was made Central Army Commander, but before he took post was transferred to Metropolitan Commandant, added Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes and credential staff, and Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs at Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, escorted the emperor back, Fu was named central army commander before he could take up the post he was shifted to metropolitan commandant, given the concurrent titles of gentleman for all purposes and credential staff, and placed in overall command at Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 帝還宮，出為平東將軍、都督揚州諸軍事，代劉准為鎮東將軍，與周玘等討陳敏，滅之，以功封永甯伯。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to the palace, Fu went out as General Who Pacifies the East, Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs of Yang province, replacing Liu Zhun as General Who Guards the East; together with Zhou Di and others he attacked Chen Min, destroyed him, and by merit was enfeoffed as Baron of Yongning.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor reached the capital again, Fu left court as General Who Pacifies the East and military governor of Yang province, succeeding Liu Zhun as General Who Guards the East; with Zhou Di and others he crushed Chen Min and earned the title Baron of Yongning.

sentences.zh: 馥自經世故，每欲維正朝遷，忠情懇至。

translations.literal: Fu himself had passed through worldly affairs and constantly wished to rectify the court's shifting, his loyal feeling earnest to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Fu had seen enough of the world's troubles and longed to steady the tottering court; his loyalty was fervent and plain.

sentences.zh: 以東海王越不盡臣節，每言論厲然，越深憚之。

translations.literal: Because the Prince of Donghai, Yue, did not exhaust ministerial propriety, in speech and discussion Fu was always stern, and Yue deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He openly reproached Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, for falling short of a subject's duty, and Yue grew deeply wary of him.

sentences.zh: 馥睹群賊孔熾，洛陽孤危，乃建策迎天子遷都壽春。

translations.literal: Fu saw the mass of bandits blazingly fierce, Luoyang orphaned and perilous, and therefore devised a plan to welcome the Son of Heaven and move the capital to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing rebel armies rage unchecked and Luoyang isolated in peril, he drew up a plan to escort the emperor and relocate the capital to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: ，與長史吳思、司馬殷識上書曰：「不圖厄運遂至於此！

translations.literal: , together with Chief Clerk Wu Si and Major Yin Shi submitted a memorial, saying: "We had not imagined that ill fortune would reach this point!
translations.idiomatic: With Chief Clerk Wu Si and Major Yin Shi he then memorialized: "We never dreamed calamity would come to this pass!

sentences.zh: 戎狄交侵，畿甸危逼。

translations.literal: Barbarians and Di mutually invade; the capital region is perilously pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Rong and Di raiders press in from every side, and the capital heartland is squeezed to breaking.

sentences.zh: 臣輒與祖納、裴憲、華譚、孫惠等三十人伏思大計，僉以殷人有屢遷之事，周王有岐山之徙，方今王都罄乏，不可久居，河朔蕭條，崤函險澀，宛都屢敗，江漢多虞，於今平夷，東南為愈。

translations.literal: Your subjects rashly with Zu Na, Pei Xian, Hua Tan, Sun Hui, and thirty others have bowed in thought on the great plan; all consider that the Yin people had the affair of repeated removals, the Zhou king had the removal to Mount Qi; now the royal capital is exhausted and cannot long be dwelt in; north of the river is desolate; Xiao and Han are perilous and obstructed; the capital of Wan has repeatedly been defeated; Jiang and Han have many alarms; at present it is level and peaceful toward the southeast, which is better.
translations.idiomatic: We, together with Zu Na, Pei Xian, Hua Tan, Sun Hui, and some thirty others, have weighed a larger strategy: the Shang kings moved their capital more than once, the Zhou kings withdrew into the Qi hills, and today Luoyang is stripped bare and cannot be held long. The north is a wasteland, the Xiao–Han passes are treacherous, Nanyang has fallen again and again, and the Jiang and Han basins are still unsettled—only the southeast is comparatively calm.

sentences.zh: 淮揚之地，北阻塗山，南抗靈嶽，名川四帶，有重險之固。

translations.literal: The land of Huai and Yang: north blocked by Tu Mountain, south confronting the numinous ranges, famous rivers girding it on four sides—it has the solidity of layered peril.
translations.idiomatic: The Huai–Yang region is shielded by Tu Mountain to the north, great ranges to the south, and four belts of major rivers—a natural fortress.

sentences.zh: 是以楚人東遷，遂宅壽春，徐邳、東海，亦足戍禦。

translations.literal: Therefore the men of Chu moved east and then dwelt at Shouchun; Xu, Pi, and Donghai also suffice for garrison defense.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the southern lords once moved east and made Shouchun their seat, while Xuzhou, Pi, and Donghai still offer enough depth to defend.

sentences.zh: 且運漕四通，無患空乏。

translations.literal: Moreover transport and grain float four ways open; there is no worry of emptiness and want.
translations.idiomatic: Grain barges can reach it from four directions, so supplies need not run dry.

sentences.zh: 雖聖上神聰，元輔賢明，居儉守約，用保宗廟，未若相土遷宅，以享永祚。

translations.literal: Although the sage superiors are divinely keen and the chief ministers worthy and bright, dwelling in frugality and keeping restraint to thereby preserve the ancestral temple, it is not as good as surveying the land and moving the residence to thereby enjoy long-lasting fortune.
translations.idiomatic: However wise the sovereign and however capable his ministers, however frugally they guard the altars, nothing matches reading the terrain and shifting the capital to secure lasting fortune.

sentences.zh: 臣謹選精卒三萬，奉迎皇駕。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully selects crack troops thirty thousand to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: We have assembled thirty thousand picked troops to escort Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 輒檄前北中郎將裴憲行使持節、監豫州諸軍事、東中郎將，風馳即路。

translations.literal: We rashly have ordered former North Army Middle General Pei Xian to act as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, oversee military affairs of Yu province, and Eastern Army Middle General; like wind galloping he takes the road.
translations.idiomatic: We have already ordered the former North Army middle general Pei Xian to take credential staff, supervise Yu province, and lead the eastern middle army—he is marching at full speed.

sentences.zh: 荊、湘、江、揚各先運四年米租十五萬斛，布絹各十四萬匹，以供大駕。

translations.literal: Jing, Xiang, Jiang, and Yang each shall first transport four years' grain rent one hundred fifty thousand hu, cloth and silk each one hundred forty thousand bolts, to supply the Grand Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, Xiang, Jiang, and Yang are each to forward four years of grain—one hundred fifty thousand hu—and one hundred forty thousand bolts each of cloth and silk for the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 令王浚、苟晞共平河朔，臣等戮力以啟南路。

translations.literal: Order Wang Jun and Gou Xi jointly to pacify the north of the river; your subjects and others will join strength to open the southern road.
translations.idiomatic: Let Wang Jun and Gou Xi together secure the Yellow River plain while we open a southern line with every force we can muster.

sentences.zh: 遷都弭寇，其計並得。

translations.literal: Moving the capital and stopping the bandits—these plans both are obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Moving the capital and crushing the raiders can be done in the same stroke.

sentences.zh: 皇輿來巡，臣宜轉據江州，以恢王略。

translations.literal: When the imperial chariot comes on tour, your subject ought to shift and occupy Jiang province to enlarge the royal strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Once Your Majesty moves, we should shift our base to Jiangzhou to extend the dynasty's strategic reach.

sentences.zh: 知無不為，古人所務，敢竭忠誠，庶報萬分。

translations.literal: To know and not to act is not done—the ancients' task; daring to exhaust loyalty and sincerity, perhaps to repay the ten thousandth part.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients held that whatever duty demands must be done; we venture this counsel in the hope of repaying the throne in some small measure.

sentences.zh: 朝遂夕隕，猶生之願。」

translations.literal: Morning established, evening fallen—still it is the wish of life."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we fall from dawn to dusk, we will count the sacrifice worthwhile."

sentences.zh: 越與苟晞不協，馥不先白於越，而直上書，越大怒。

translations.literal: Yue and Gou Xi were not in harmony; Fu did not first report to Yue but went straight to memorializing; Yue was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Because Sima Yue and Gou Xi were at odds, Fu bypassed Yue and sent the memorial straight to the throne; Yue was furious.

sentences.zh: 先是，越召馥及淮南太守裴碩，馥不肯行，而令碩率兵先進。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yue had summoned Fu and the Administrator of Huainan, Pei Shuo; Fu was unwilling to go, but ordered Shuo to lead troops and advance first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yue had summoned Fu and Pei Shuo, administrator of Huainan; Fu stalled but told Shuo to march ahead with the troops.

sentences.zh: 碩貳於馥，乃舉兵稱馥擅命，已奉越密旨圖馥，遂襲之，為馥所敗。

translations.literal: Shuo was divided in loyalty toward Fu, then raised troops declaring Fu had usurped command, that he had received Yue's secret edict to plot against Fu, then attacked him, and was defeated by Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo turned on Fu, raised troops accusing him of acting without orders, claimed he had Yue's secret warrant to move against him, and attacked—but Fu defeated him.

sentences.zh: 碩退保東城，求救於元帝。

translations.literal: Shuo withdrew to protect Dongcheng and sought rescue from the Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo fell back to Dongcheng and appealed for help to Sima Rui, the Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 帝遣揚威將軍甘卓、建威將軍郭逸攻馥于壽春。

translations.literal: The Prince sent General Who Displays Might Gan Zhuo and General Who Establishes Might Guo Yi to attack Fu at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: The prince dispatched Gan Zhuo, General Who Displays Might, and Guo Yi, General Who Establishes Might, to strike Fu at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 安豐太守孫惠帥眾應之，使謝摛為檄。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Anfeng, Sun Hui, led the masses to respond to him and had Xie Chi draft a proclamation.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, administrator of Anfeng, brought his troops over to their side and had Xie Chi compose the call to arms.

sentences.zh: 摛，馥之故將也。

translations.literal: Chi was Fu's former general.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chi had once served under Fu.

sentences.zh: 馥見檄，流涕曰：「必謝摛之辭。

translations.literal: When Fu saw the proclamation, he wept and said: "It must be Chi's wording.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu read the proclamation he wept and said, "Only Xie Chi could have written this.

sentences.zh: 」摛聞之，遂毀草。

translations.literal: " When Chi heard it, then destroyed the draft.
translations.idiomatic: When Chi heard that, he destroyed his draft.

sentences.zh: 旬日而馥眾潰，奔于項，為新蔡王確所拘，憂憤發病卒。

translations.literal: Within ten days Fu's host collapsed; he fled to Xiang, was detained by the Prince of Xincai, Que, and in worry and resentment fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: Within days Fu's army melted away; he fled to Xiang, was seized by Sima Que, Prince of Xincai, and died of grief and rage in captivity.

sentences.zh: 初，華譚之失廬江也，往壽春依馥，及馥軍敗，歸於元帝。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Hua Tan had lost Lujiang, he went to Shouchun and relied on Fu; when Fu's army was defeated, he returned to the Prince of Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Hua Tan lost Lujiang, he had taken refuge with Fu at Shouchun; when Fu fell, he went over to Sima Rui.

sentences.zh: 帝問曰：「周祖宣何至於反？

translations.literal: The Prince asked, saying: "How did Zhou Zuxuan reach the point of rebelling?
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked, "How did Zhou Fu come to be called a rebel?"

sentences.zh: 」譚封曰：「周馥雖死，天下尚有直言之士。

translations.literal: Tan replied: Though Zhou Fu is dead, the empire still has men who speak straight.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Tan replied, "Zhou Fu is dead, but the realm still has men willing to speak plain truth.

sentences.zh: 馥見寇賊滋蔓，王威不振，故欲移都以紓國難。

translations.literal: Fu saw invaders and bandits spreading and flourishing, royal awesomeness not roused, and therefore wished to move the capital to loosen the state's difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: He saw rebels overrun the country and royal authority fail, and wanted to move the capital to ease the dynasty's peril.

sentences.zh: 方伯不同，遂致其伐。

translations.literal: The regional shepherds did not agree, and therefore brought about this attack on him.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commanders disagreed with him, and that brought the armies down on him.

sentences.zh: 曾不逾時，而京都淪沒。

translations.literal: In not more than passing time, the capital district was sunk and lost.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luoyang itself fell.

sentences.zh: 若使從馥之謀，或可後亡也。

translations.literal: If we had followed Fu's plan, perhaps we could have perished later.
translations.idiomatic: Had the court followed his plan, the catastrophe might have come later—if at all.

sentences.zh: 原情求實，何得為反！

translations.literal: Tracing feeling and seeking the real—how can this count as rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh the facts: how can anyone call that rebellion?

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「馥位為征鎮，握兵方隅，召而不入，危而不持，亦天下之罪人也。

translations.literal: " The Prince said: "Fu's position was as zhen and garrison commander, grasping troops in a corner of the realm; summoned yet not entering, in peril yet not holding—he also is a guilty man of the empire.
translations.idiomatic: The prince answered: "He held a border command and an army; when summoned he would not come, and in crisis he would not stand firm—he too bears the realm's blame.

sentences.zh: 」譚曰：「然。

translations.literal: Tan said: So.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "That is true.

sentences.zh: 馥振纓中朝，素有俊彥之稱；

translations.literal: Fu shook his tassels in the central court and always had the reputation of an outstanding talent;
translations.idiomatic: At court he had long been praised as a leading talent;

sentences.zh: 出據方嶽，實有偏任之重，而高略不舉，往往失和，危而不持，當與天下共受其責。

translations.literal: going out to occupy a regional peak, he truly had the weight of partial commission, yet high strategy he did not raise, repeatedly lost harmony, in peril did not hold—he ought with the empire together to bear the blame.
translations.idiomatic: sent out to a great regional command, he bore heavy responsibility, yet he never carried through a larger strategy, often quarreled with peers, and failed to hold the line in danger—he must share the blame with everyone else.

sentences.zh: 然謂之反，不亦誣乎！

translations.literal: Yet to call it rebellion—is it not slander!
translations.idiomatic: Still, to brand him a traitor is sheer calumny!"

sentences.zh: 」帝意始解。

translations.literal: " The Prince's intent then loosened.
translations.idiomatic: The prince's anger eased.

sentences.zh: 馥有二子：密、矯。

translations.literal: Fu had two sons: Mi and Jiao.
translations.idiomatic: Fu left two sons, Mi and Jiao.

sentences.zh: 密字泰玄，性虛簡，時人稱為清士，位至尚書郎，矯字正玄，亦有才幹。

translations.literal: Mi, courtesy name Taixuan, by nature was empty and simple; people of the time called him a pure gentleman; he reached Gentleman of the Masters of Writing. Jiao, courtesy name Zhengxuan, also had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Mi, courtesy name Taixuan, was modest and retiring and was known as a man of integrity; he rose to gentleman of the Masters of Writing. Jiao, courtesy name Zhengxuan, was capable in office as well.

sentences.zh: 成公簡

translations.literal: Cheng Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongjian

sentences.zh: 成公簡，字宗舒，東郡人也。

translations.literal: Cheng Gongjian, courtesy name Zongshu, was a man of Dong commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Gongjian, courtesy name Zongshu, came from Dong commandery.

sentences.zh: 家世二千石。

translations.literal: His family for generations held two-thousand-dan rank.
translations.idiomatic: His family had held ministerial rank for generations.

sentences.zh: 性樸素，不求榮利，潛心味道，罔有幹其志者。

translations.literal: By nature he was plain and simple, did not seek glory and profit, submerged his heart in tasting the Way; none had what could interfere with his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He was plain and unworldly, indifferent to rank and profit, and gave himself wholly to the Way, letting nothing distract him.

sentences.zh: 默識過人。

translations.literal: Silent recognition surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: His memory and silent learning were extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 張茂先每言：「簡清靜比楊子雲，默識擬張安世。

translations.literal: Zhang Maoxian always said: "Jian's cleanness and stillness may be compared to Yang Ziyun; silent recognition may be paired with Zhang Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua used to say, "In quiet purity Gongjian matches Yang Xiong; in retentive memory he rivals Zhang Anshi."

sentences.zh: 」後為中書郎。

translations.literal: Later he became Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as gentleman of the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時馥已為司隸校尉，遷鎮東將軍。

translations.literal: At the time Fu already was Metropolitan Commandant and had been transferred to General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhou Fu was metropolitan commandant and had been promoted to General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 簡自以才高而在馥之下，謂馥曰：「揚雄為郎，三世不徙，而王莽、董賢位列三司，古今一揆耳。

translations.literal: Jian himself considered his talent high yet was below Fu; he said to Fu: "Yang Xiong as a gentleman thrice generations did not move, yet Wang Mang and Dong Xian ranked in the Three Offices—antiquity and today are one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Gongjian thought his gifts outranked Fu's yet he stood below him in the table of ranks, and told him, "Yang Xiong remained a court gentleman for three reigns without promotion while Wang Mang and Dong Xian vaulted to the three highest offices—the past and present rhyme the same way."

sentences.zh: 」馥甚慚之。

translations.literal: Fu was very ashamed toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was deeply embarrassed.

sentences.zh: 官至太子中庶子、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: His office reached Household Supervisor of the Heir Apparent and Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to household supervisor of the heir apparent and gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 永嘉末，奔苟晞，與晞同沒。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongjia era he fled to Gou Xi and perished together with Xi.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the Yongjia era he fled to Gou Xi and died with him.

sentences.zh: 苟晞

translations.literal: Gou Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi

sentences.zh: 苟晞，字道將，河內山陽人也。

translations.literal: Gou Xi, courtesy name Daojiang, was a man of Shanyang in Henan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi, courtesy name Daojiang, came from Shanyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 少為司隸部從事，校尉石鑒深器之。

translations.literal: In youth he was an attendant clerk in the Metropolitan Commandant's department; Commandant Shi Jian deeply prized him.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk under the metropolitan commandant, and Commandant Shi Jian thought the world of him.

sentences.zh: 東海王越為侍中，引為通事令史，累遷陽平太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Donghai, Yue, was Palace Attendant, he brought him in as Master of Documents for General Affairs, and by successive promotions he reached Administrator of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, was palace attendant, he took Xi on as master of documents for general affairs, and Xi rose to administrator of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏輔政，晞參冏軍事，拜尚書右丞，轉左丞，廉察諸曹，八坐以下皆側目憚之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Jiong, assisted the government, Xi participated in Jiong's military affairs, was appointed Right Assistant in the Masters of Writing, transferred to Left Assistant, inspected all bureaus, and from the Eight Seats downward all sidelong-eyed feared him.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Sima Jiong of Qi directed the government, Xi served on his military staff, then became right assistant in the Masters of Writing and shifted to left assistant; his audits of every bureau had even senior ministers watching him sideways in fear.

sentences.zh: 及冏誅，晞亦坐免。

translations.literal: When Jiong was executed, Xi also by sitting was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong was executed, Xi lost his post as an associate.

sentences.zh: 長沙王乂為驃騎將軍，以晞為從事中郎。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Changsha, Yi, was Cavalry-in-Ordinary General, he made Xi Staff Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Sima Yi of Changsha was cavalry-in-ordinary general, he appointed Xi staff supervisor.

sentences.zh: 惠帝征成都王穎，以為北軍中候。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui campaigned against the Prince of Chengdu, Ying, he made him North Army Middle Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Hui's expedition against Sima Ying, Prince of Chengdu, Xi was named North Army middle commander.

sentences.zh: 及帝還洛陽，晞奔范陽王虓，虓承制用晞行兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When the Emperor returned to Luoyang, Xi fled to the Prince of Fanyang, Xiao, and Xiao by interim authority employed Xi to act as Inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to Luoyang, Xi joined Sima Xiao, Prince of Fanyang, who by interim warrant put him in charge as acting inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 汲桑之破鄴也，東海王越出次官渡以討之，命晞為前鋒。

translations.literal: When Ji Sang broke Ye, the Prince of Donghai, Yue, went out and halted at Guandu to attack him, and ordered Xi as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji Sang sacked Ye, Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, encamped at Guandu to strike him and named Xi vanguard.

sentences.zh: 桑素憚之，於城外為柵以自守。

translations.literal: Sang always feared him; outside the city he made palisades to guard himself.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang, who had long feared him, threw up palisades outside the city.

sentences.zh: 晞將至，頓軍休士，先遣單騎示以禍福。

translations.literal: As Xi was about to arrive, he halted the army and rested the troops, first sending a lone rider to show them fortune and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before closing in, Xi rested his troops and sent a lone rider to spell out surrender or ruin.

sentences.zh: 桑眾大震，棄柵宵遁，嬰城固守。

translations.literal: Sang's host was greatly shaken, abandoned the palisades and fled by night, and ringed the city firmly defending.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Sang’s army panicked, abandoned the stockade, fled by night, and then locked themselves inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 晞陷其九壘，遂定鄴而還。

translations.literal: Xi broke through his nine ramparts, thereupon pacified Ye and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Xi stormed nine fortified camps, pacified Ye, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 西討呂朗等，滅之。

translations.literal: He campaigned west against Lu Lang and others and destroyed them.
translations.idiomatic: He marched west, crushed Lu Lang and allied bands, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 後高密王泰討青州賊劉根，破汲桑故將公師籓，敗石勒于河北，威名甚盛，時人擬之韓白。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Gaomi, Tai, campaigned against the Qingzhou bandit Liu Gen, broke Ji Sang’s former general Gongshi Fan, defeated Shi Le north of the river—his awe-inspiring name was very great, and people of the time compared him to Han Xin and Bai Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Sima Tai of Gaomi campaigned against the Qingzhou rebel Liu Gen, broke Gongshi Fan, a former lieutenant of Ji Sang, and defeated Shi Le north of the Yellow River; his reputation was so formidable that contemporaries likened him to Han Xin and Bai Qi.

sentences.zh: 進位撫軍將軍、假節、都督青兗諸軍事，封東平郡侯，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to General Who Pacifies the Army, credential staff, Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs of Qing and Yan provinces, enfeoffed as Marquis of Dongping commandery with ten thousand households’ fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Army with credential staff, military governor of Qing and Yan, and enfeoffed as marquis of Dongping with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 晞練于官事，文簿盈積，斷決如流，人不敢欺。

translations.literal: Xi was practiced in official affairs; documents and ledgers piled full; he decided judgments like flowing water, and people did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was a master administrator: his desk overflowed with papers, yet he cleared cases like running water and no one dared deceive him.

sentences.zh: 其從母依之，奉養甚厚。

translations.literal: His aunt by marriage relied on him, and he supported her very generously.
translations.idiomatic: A widowed aunt lived under his roof, and he supported her lavishly.

sentences.zh: 從母子求為將，晞距之曰：「吾不以王法貸人，將無後悔邪？

translations.literal: The son of his aunt by marriage sought to become a general; Xi refused him, saying: "I do not by royal law lend favor to people—you will have no later regret?"
translations.idiomatic: Her son asked for a command; Xi refused: "I do not bend the law for kin—will you not regret pressing me?"

sentences.zh: 」固欲之，晞乃以為督護。

translations.literal: He firmly wished it; Xi then made him a protector.
translations.idiomatic: The youth insisted, and Xi relented and named him a protector.

sentences.zh: 後犯法，晞杖節斬之，從母叩頭請救，不聽。

translations.literal: Later he violated the law; Xi with staff and credentials beheaded him; his aunt by marriage knocked her head begging rescue; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When the nephew broke the law, Xi executed him in full regalia; his aunt pleaded in vain.

sentences.zh: 既而素服哭之，流涕曰：「殺卿者兗州刺史，哭弟者苟道將。

translations.literal: Afterward in plain mourning he wept for him, shedding tears and saying: "The one who killed you was the Inspector of Yan; the one who weeps for a younger brother is Gou Daojiang."
translations.idiomatic: Then, dressed in mourning for a commoner, he wept and said, "The inspector of Yan province passed sentence; your elder brother Gou Daojiang weeps for you."

sentences.zh: 」其杖法如此。

translations.literal: Thus was his wielding of law.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his ruthlessness under the law.

sentences.zh: 晞見朝政日亂，懼禍及己，而多所交結，每得珍物，即貽都下親貴。

translations.literal: Xi saw court government daily in disorder, feared disaster reaching himself, and therefore made many connections; whenever he obtained rare treasures, he then presented them to kin and nobles in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the court slide into chaos, Xi feared being dragged down and cultivated the great families of Luoyang with lavish gifts whenever he acquired rare goods.

sentences.zh: 兗州去洛五百里，恐不鮮美，募得千里牛，每遣信，旦發暮還。

translations.literal: Yan province was five hundred li from Luoyang; fearing things were not fresh and fine, he recruited oxen that could go a thousand li a day; whenever he sent a messenger, they set out at dawn and returned at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Yan province lay five hundred li from the capital, so he requisitioned legendary long-distance ox carts that could deliver fresh delicacies from his camp to Luoyang between dawn and dusk.

sentences.zh: 初，東海王越以晞復其仇恥，甚德之，引升堂，結為兄弟。

translations.literal: Earlier the Prince of Donghai, Yue, because Xi avenged his shame and hatred, greatly favored him, led him up the hall, and bonded as brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, regarded Xi as the man who had avenged his humiliation and treated him like a sworn brother, even receiving him in the inner hall.

sentences.zh: 越司馬潘滔等說曰：「兗州要衝，魏武以之輔相漢室。

translations.literal: Yue's Major Pan Tao and others urged him, saying: "Yan province is a vital chokepoint; Wei Wu used it to assist the Han house."
translations.idiomatic: His major, Pan Tao, warned him: "Yan province is the pivot of the realm—the seat from which Cao Cao once steadied the Han."

sentences.zh: 苟晞有大志，非純臣，久令處之，則患生心腹矣。

translations.literal: Gou Xi has great intent; he is not a pure minister; long letting him occupy it, then disaster will be born in the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi harbors larger ambitions than a loyal minister should; leave him there too long and he will become a dagger at your own breast.

sentences.zh: 若遷於青州，厚其名號，晞必悅，公自牧兗州，經緯諸夏，籓衛本朝，此所謂謀之於未有，為之於未亂也。

translations.literal: If you transfer him to Qing province and enrich his title and name, Xi will surely be pleased; you yourself will shepherd Yan province, regulate the myriad Xia, and screen the root court—this is what is called plotting before it exists and acting before it is chaotic.
translations.idiomatic: Shift him to Qingzhou with a grander title and he will be mollified; you yourself can hold Yan province, knit the central plains together, and shield the throne—true "planning before the crisis" and "acting before the rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」越以為然，乃遷晞征東大將軍、開府儀同三司，加侍中、假節、都督青州諸軍事，領青州刺史，進為郡公。

translations.literal: Yue deemed it right, then transferred Xi to General Who Conquers the East, opening office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies, added Palace Attendant, credential staff, Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs of Qing province, concurrently Inspector of Qing province, and advanced to commandery duke.
translations.idiomatic: Yue agreed: Xi was promoted to General Who Conquers the East with independent headquarters and three excellencies–rank ceremony, made palace attendant with credential staff, military governor of Qing province, concurrent inspector of Qing province, and elevated to a commandery duke.

sentences.zh: 晞乃多置參佐，轉易守令，以嚴刻立功，日加斬戮，流血成川，人不堪命，號曰「屠伯」。

translations.literal: Xi then greatly increased adjutants, rotated and replaced prefects and magistrates, by severity and harshness achieved merit, daily added executions and killings, flowing blood became rivers, people could not bear the mandate, and he was called "Butcher Earl."
translations.idiomatic: Xi then packed his staff with hatchet men, shuffled every local magistrate, and ruled through terror—executions mounted until blood ran in streams; the people could not endure him and nicknamed him the "Butcher Earl."

sentences.zh: 頓丘太守魏植為流人所逼，眾五六萬，大掠兗州。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Dunqiu, Wei Zhi, was pressed by displaced people; his crowd was fifty or sixty thousand and greatly plundered Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhi, administrator of Dunqiu, was overrun by fifty or sixty thousand displaced people who pillaged Yan province.

sentences.zh: 晞出屯無鹽，以弟純領青州，刑殺更甚于晞，百姓號「小苟酷于大苟」。

translations.literal: Xi went out and encamped at Wuyan, with his younger brother Chun heading Qing province; punishments and killings were even more severe than Xi’s; the common people called it "Little Gou is crueller than Great Gou."
translations.idiomatic: Xi marched to Wuyan while his brother Chun held Qing province; Chun’s killings outdid his own, and folk said, "The younger Gou is crueler than the elder."

sentences.zh: 晞尋破植。

translations.literal: Soon Xi broke Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi soon smashed Wei Zhi’s host.

sentences.zh: 時潘滔及尚書劉望等共誣陷晞，晞怒，表求滔等首，又請越從事中郎劉洽為軍司，越皆不許。

translations.literal: At the time Pan Tao and Masters of Writing Liu Wang and others together slandered and framed Xi; Xi was angry, memorialized demanding Tao and others’ heads, and also requested Yue’s Staff Supervisor Liu Qia as army director; Yue all did not grant.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Tao, Liu Wang, and other ministers slandered Gou Xi; he retaliated with a memorial demanding their heads and asked to place Liu Qia of Yue’s staff over his army—Sima Yue refused every point.

sentences.zh: 晞於是昌言曰：「司馬元超為宰相不平，使天下淆亂，苟道將豈可以不義使之？

translations.literal: Xi then openly declared, saying: "Sima Yuanchao as chief minister is not fair, causing the empire to be in confusion and chaos—how can Gou Daojiang be driven by unrighteousness?
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi then declared openly, "Sima Yue sits as chief minister yet throws the realm into chaos—do you think Gou Daojiang can be ordered about unjustly?

sentences.zh: 韓信不忍衣食之惠，死於婦人之手。

translations.literal: Han Xin could not bear the kindness of clothes and food and died in a woman’s hands.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xin could not resist small favors and died at a woman’s hands.

sentences.zh: 今將誅國賊，尊王室，桓文豈遠哉！

translations.literal: Now I shall execute the traitors to the state and honor the royal house—are Huan and Wen far!
translations.idiomatic: I mean to execute the traitors and restore the throne—the age of Duke Huan and Duke Wen is not far off!

sentences.zh: 」乃移告諸州，稱己功伐，陳越罪狀。

translations.literal: " Then he shifted notice to the various provinces, proclaiming his own merit, and setting forth Yue’s crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He then circulated proclamations through every province, trumpeting his own victories and listing Sima Yue’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 時懷帝惡越專權，乃詔晞曰：「朕以不德，戎車屢興，上懼宗廟之累，下湣兆庶之困，當賴方岳，為國籓翰。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Huai detested Yue’s monopolizing power, then edicted to Xi, saying: "We by lack of virtue have war chariots repeatedly raised; above We fear burden on the ancestral temple, below We pity the black-haired people’s distress—We ought to rely on regional peaks as the state’s screen and stem.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai, resenting Sima Yue’s monopoly of power, sent Gou Xi an edict: "Lacking virtue, We have brought repeated war; We fear for the altars above and pity the people below, and must lean on great regional commanders as bulwarks of the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 公威震赫然，梟斬籓、桑，走降喬、朗，魏植之徒復以誅除，豈非高識明斷，朕用委成。

translations.literal: Your awe-inspiring might shakes brilliantly; you have beheaded Fan and Sang as owls, put Qiao and Lang to flight and submission, and Wei Zhi’s sort again by execution removed—is this not high insight and clear judgment? We therefore entrust completion to you.
translations.idiomatic: Your prestige is formidable: you beheaded Gongshi Fan and Ji Sang, routed and accepted the surrender of Qiao and Lang, and wiped out men like Wei Zhi—surely that is foresight and resolve; We therefore place full trust in you.

sentences.zh: 加王彌、石勒為社稷之憂，故有詔委統六州。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Mi and Shi Le are worry for the altars of soil and grain; therefore there is an edict commissioning you to command six provinces.
translations.idiomatic: With Wang Mi and Shi Le threatening the state, We have ordered you to coordinate six provinces.

sentences.zh: 而公謙分小節，稽違大命，非所謂與國同憂也。

translations.literal: Yet you modestly divide yourself on small points and delay the great mandate—this is not what is called sharing worry with the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you cling to petty scruples and stall on the great commission—that is not how a loyal bulwark shares the dynasty’s peril.

sentences.zh: 今復遣詔，便施檄六州，協同大舉，翦除國難，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: Now again We send edict; immediately issue summons to six provinces, join in the great rising, cut away the state’s difficulty, to match Our intent.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore repeat Our order: issue calls across six provinces, join in a concerted campaign, and remove this mortal threat to the realm—that is Our wish.

sentences.zh: 」晞復移諸征鎮州郡曰：

translations.literal: " Xi again shifted notice to the various zhen, garrison, province, and commandery, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi followed with another circular to every provincial and garrison command:

sentences.zh: 會王彌遣曹嶷破琅邪，北攻齊地。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Mi sent Cao Yi to break Langya and attack north into Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Wang Mi sent Cao Yi to storm Langya and drive north into Qi.

sentences.zh: 苟純城守，嶷眾轉盛，連營數十里。

translations.literal: Gou Chun defended the city; Yi’s host grew ever stronger, connecting camps for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Chun held the walls while Cao Yi’s army swelled into linked camps dozens of li long.

sentences.zh: 晞還，登城望之，有懼色，與賊連戰，輒破之。

translations.literal: Xi returned, ascended the city and looked on them, had a frightened color, and with the bandits fought successive battles, always breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: When Gou Xi came back and mounted the wall he blanched at the sight, yet in skirmish after skirmish he still broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 後簡精銳，與賊大戰，會大風揚塵，遂敗績，棄城夜走。

translations.literal: Later he picked crack troops and fought a great battle with the bandits; it happened that great wind raised dust, then he was routed, abandoned the city and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He later led picked troops into a major battle, but a dust storm blinded his lines, his army collapsed, and he abandoned the city by night.

sentences.zh: 嶷追至東山，部眾皆降嶷。

translations.literal: Yi pursued to Dongshan; the division’s host all surrendered to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Yi pursued him to Dongshan, where Gou Xi’s men went over to the enemy wholesale.

sentences.zh: 晞單騎奔高平，收邸閣，募得數千人。

translations.literal: Xi alone on horseback fled to Gaoping, collected granary posts, and recruited several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi rode alone to Gaoping, seized government storehouses, and scraped together a few thousand followers.

sentences.zh: 帝又密詔晞討越，晞復上表曰：

translations.literal: The Emperor again secretly edicted Xi to campaign against Yue; Xi again submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent another secret order for him to strike Sima Yue, and Gou Xi answered with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 五年，帝復詔晞曰：「太傅信用奸佞，阻兵專權，內不遵奉皇憲，外不協比方州，遂令戎狄充斥，所在犯暴。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor again edicted to Xi, saying: "The Grand Tutor trusts wicked flatterers, blocks troops and monopolizes power; within he does not reverently obey the royal statutes, without he does not harmonize with the provinces; thereupon he has let Rong and Di fill and overflow, wherever they go committing violence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor wrote again: "The grand tutor trusts villains, keeps armies under private control, flouts imperial law at court and refuses to work with the provinces abroad, until Rong and Di raiders overrun the land.

sentences.zh: 留軍何倫抄掠宮寺，劫剝公主，殺害賢士，悖亂天下，不可忍聞。

translations.literal: He left troops under He Lun plundering palace monasteries, robbing princesses, killing worthy gentlemen—rebellious disorder under Heaven, unbearable to hear.
translations.idiomatic: He Lun’s detachment loots monasteries, robs princesses, murders worthies—outrages no loyal ear can bear.

sentences.zh: 雖惟親親，宜明九伐。

translations.literal: Although We think only of kin, it is fitting to clarify the nine punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Kinship cannot excuse him: the statutes provide for traitors.

sentences.zh: 詔至之日，其宣告天下，率齊大舉，桓文之績，一以委公。

translations.literal: When the edict arrives, proclaim it to the empire, gather for the great rising—the deeds of Huan and Wen We wholly entrust to the duke.
translations.idiomatic: When this edict goes out, proclaim it to the realm, muster the hosts, and finish what Dukes Huan and Wen began—We lay that charge on you.

sentences.zh: 其思盡諸宜，善建弘略。

translations.literal: Think through every suitable measure and well establish a grand plan.
translations.idiomatic: Think through every detail and lay a strategy worthy of the charge.

sentences.zh: 道澀，故練寫副，手筆示意。

translations.literal: The roads are obstructed; therefore We have practiced writing a duplicate copy, by hand brush indicating intent.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads are unsafe We enclose a fair copy in Our own brush to show Our mind."

sentences.zh: 」晞表曰：「奉被手詔，委臣征討，喻以桓文，紙練兼備，伏讀跪歎，五情惶怛。

translations.literal: " Xi memorialized, saying: "We have received the brush edict commissioning your subject to campaign and punish, instructing with Huan and Wen; paper and duplicate are both complete; kneeling We read and sigh, the five feelings are anxious and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi replied: "I have received Your Majesty’s autograph commissioning me to punish the traitors, invoking the model of Dukes Huan and Wen; holding the duplicate copy I knelt, read, and trembled with awe.

sentences.zh: 自頃宰臣專制，委杖佞邪，內擅朝威，外殘兆庶，矯詔專征，遂圖不軌，縱兵寇掠，陵踐宮寺。

translations.literal: From of late chief ministers have monopolized power, entrusted staffs to flattering evil, within usurp court awesomeness, without mutilate the black-haired people, forged edicts to wage private wars, then plotted unorthodox courses, let loose troops to raid and plunder, trampling palace monasteries.
translations.idiomatic: For years chief ministers have seized power, handed staff to sycophants, bullied the court and butchered the people, forged orders for private wars, harbored treason, and let soldiers sack even palace chapels.

sentences.zh: 前司隸校尉劉暾、御史中丞溫畿、右將軍杜育，並見攻劫。

translations.literal: Former Metropolitan Commandant Liu Tun, Palace Assistant Secretary Wen Ji, and General Who Guards the Right Du Yu were together attacked and robbed.
translations.idiomatic: The former metropolitan commandant Liu Tun, palace assistant secretary Wen Ji, and General Who Guards the Right Du Yu were all robbed under arms.

sentences.zh: 廣平、武安公主，先帝遺體，咸被逼辱。

translations.literal: The Princesses of Guangping and Wu’an, the late Emperor’s bodily relics, were both forced to shame.
translations.idiomatic: Even the princesses of Guangping and Wu’an—daughters of the late emperor—were violated.

sentences.zh: 逆節虐亂，莫此之甚。

translations.literal: Rebellious principle, cruel disorder—none surpasses this.
translations.idiomatic: Treason has never sunk lower.

sentences.zh: 輒祗奉前詔，部分諸軍，遣王贊率陳午等將兵詣項，龔行天罰。」

translations.literal: We rashly have reverently received the former edict, divided and arranged the various armies, sent Wang Zan leading Chen Wu and others to lead troops to Xiang, respectfully to carry out Heaven’s punishment."
translations.idiomatic: I therefore obey the earlier edict, array the armies, and dispatch Wang Zan with Chen Wu and others toward Xiang to carry out Heaven’s sentence."

sentences.zh: 初，越疑晞與帝有謀，使游騎于成阜間，獲晞使，果得詔令及朝廷書，遂大構疑隙。

translations.literal: Earlier Yue suspected Xi had plotting with the Emperor, sent roaming riders between Chenggao, captured Xi’s messenger, and indeed obtained edict orders and court letters, thereupon greatly built suspicion and rift.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue had suspected secret traffic between Gou Xi and the throne; patrols between Chenggao seized Gou Xi’s courier and found the palace letters, which opened a fatal breach between them.

sentences.zh: 越出牧豫州以討晞，復下檄說晞罪惡，遣從事中郎楊瑁為兗州，與徐州刺史裴盾共討晞。

translations.literal: Yue went out to shepherd Yu province to campaign against Xi, again issued summons stating Xi’s crimes and evils, sent Staff Supervisor Yang Mao as Yan province, and together with Xu province Inspector Pei Dun jointly campaigned against Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue left Luoyang to take Yu province in person against Gou Xi, published a bill of particulars, named Yang Mao acting inspector of Yan, and joined Pei Dun, inspector of Xu, in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 晞使騎收河南尹潘滔，滔夜遁，及執尚書劉會、侍中程延，斬之。

translations.literal: Xi sent riders to seize Henan Intendant Pan Tao; Tao fled by night, and when he seized Masters of Writing Liu Hui and Palace Attendant Cheng Yan, he beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi sent horsemen to arrest Pan Tao, intendant of Henan; Pan escaped by night, but Liu Hui of the Masters of Writing and palace attendant Cheng Yan were taken and executed.

sentences.zh: 會越薨，盾敗，詔晞為大將軍大都督、督青徐兗豫荊揚六州諸軍事，增邑二萬戶，加黃鉞，先官如故。

translations.literal: When it happened that Yue died, Dun was defeated; an edict made Xi Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, commander of military affairs in Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang provinces, increased fief by twenty thousand households, added yellow axe, prior offices as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue died and Pei Dun collapsed, the court named Gou Xi grand general and overall commander of six provinces, added twenty thousand households to his fief, gave him the yellow axe, and left his other titles intact.

sentences.zh: 晞以京邑荒饉日甚，寇難交至，表請遷都，遣從事中郎劉會領船數十艘，宿衛五百人，獻穀千斛以迎帝。

translations.literal: Xi because the capital district famine grew daily worse and bandit calamity arrived together, memorialized requesting to move the capital, sent Staff Supervisor Liu Hui to lead several tens of ships, five hundred palace guards, and present a thousand hu of grain to welcome the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Luoyang starving and besieged, he asked to evacuate the court, sent Liu Hui with dozens of transports, five hundred guards, and a thousand hu of grain to bring the emperor out.

sentences.zh: 朝臣多有異同。

translations.literal: Court ministers for the most part had differing agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers were deeply divided.

sentences.zh: 俄而京師陷，晞與王贊屯倉垣。

translations.literal: Soon the capital fell; Xi with Wang Zan encamped at Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang soon fell; Gou Xi and Wang Zan held Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 豫章王端及和鬱等東奔晞，晞群官尊端為皇太子，置行台。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuzhang, Duan, and He Yu and others fled east to Xi; Xi’s host of officials honored Duan as imperial heir apparent and set up a mobile secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Duan, Prince of Yuzhang, fled east to his camp; Gou Xi’s officers hailed him as crown prince and set up a traveling administration.

sentences.zh: 端承制以晞領太子太傅、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書，自倉垣徙屯蒙城，贊屯陽夏。

translations.literal: Duan by interim authority made Xi concurrent Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, commander of all military affairs within and without, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; from Cangyuan he shifted encampment to Mengcheng, Zan encamped at Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Duan appointed Gou Xi grand tutor to the heir apparent, overall commander, and supervisor of the Masters of Writing, moved from Cangyuan to Mengcheng, and stationed Wang Zan at Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 晞出於孤微，位至上將，志頗盈滿，奴婢將千人，侍妾數十，終日累夜不出戶庭，刑政苛虐，縱情肆欲。

translations.literal: Xi came from orphan humble status, reached position of highest general, his intent quite full; slave girls and household servants nearly a thousand, serving concubines several tens; all day piled night he did not go out doors and courtyard; punishments and government harsh and cruel, indulging feeling and wanton desire.
translations.idiomatic: Raised from nothing to the empire’s highest command, Gou Xi grew arrogant: nearly a thousand slaves, dozens of concubines, he rarely left his compound, and his justice turned savage and capricious.

sentences.zh: 遼西閻亨以書固諫，晞怒，殺之。
