translations.literal: Yan Heng of Liaoxi with a letter firmly remonstrated; Xi was angry and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Heng of Liaoxi remonstrated firmly in writing; Gou Xi had him killed.

sentences.zh: 晞從事中郎明預有疾居家，聞之，乃舉病諫晞曰：「皇晉遭百六之數，當危難之機，明公親稟廟算，將為國家除暴。

translations.literal: Xi’s Staff Supervisor Ming Yu had illness and dwelt at home; hearing it, he then raised his illness to remonstrate Xi, saying: "The imperial Jin has met the hundred-six’s reckoning, is at crisis’s pivot; the enlightened duke personally bears the temple’s plan and will for the state remove violence.
translations.idiomatic: His staff supervisor Ming Yu, ill at home, dragged himself up to say, "The house of Jin faces its worst hour; you hold the dynasty’s strategy and mean to crush the rebels.

sentences.zh: 閻亨美士，奈何無罪一旦殺之！

translations.literal: Yan Heng was a fine gentleman—how without guilt in one morning kill him!
translations.idiomatic: Yan Heng was a good man—why murder him without cause?

sentences.zh: 」晞怒白；

translations.literal: Xi angrily declared;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi snarled back,

sentences.zh: 「我自殺閻亨，何關人事，而舉病來罵我！

translations.literal: "I myself killed Yan Heng—what does it concern others’ affairs, that you raise illness to come curse me!
translations.idiomatic: "I killed Yan Heng myself—what is it to you that you limp here to insult me?

sentences.zh: 」左右為之戰慄，預曰：「以明公以禮見進，預欲以禮自盡。

translations.literal: " Those at his sides for it trembled; Yu said: "Because the enlightened duke advanced me by ritual, Yu wished to repay with ritual even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants shook with fear; Ming Yu said, "You honored me with courtesy; I meant to answer with courtesy unto death.

sentences.zh: 今明公怒預，其若遠近怒明公何！

translations.literal: Now the enlightened duke is angry at Yu—how about the near and far being angry at the enlightened duke!
translations.idiomatic: Now you rage at me—what will you do when the whole country rages at you?

sentences.zh: 昔堯舜之在上也，以和理而興；

translations.literal: In antiquity when Yao and Shun were above, by harmony and order they rose;
translations.idiomatic: When Yao and Shun ruled, harmony built their power;

sentences.zh: 桀紂之在上也，以惡逆而滅。

translations.literal: when Jie and Zhou were above, by wicked rebellion they perished.
translations.idiomatic: when Jie and Zhou ruled, cruelty destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 天子且猶如此，況人臣乎！

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven is still thus—how much more a subject!
translations.idiomatic: If even sovereigns are judged so, what of mere ministers?

sentences.zh: 願明公且置其怒而思預之言。

translations.literal: I wish the enlightened duke for the moment set aside his anger and ponder Yu’s words.
translations.idiomatic: Set aside your anger and weigh what I have said."

sentences.zh: 」晞有慚色。

translations.literal: " Xi had a shameful color.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi colored with shame.

sentences.zh: 由是眾心稍離，莫為致用，加以疾疫饑饉，其將溫畿、傅宣皆叛之。

translations.literal: From this the host’s hearts gradually departed; none acted for him to use; added to that were plague, famine, and his generals Wen Ji and Fu Xuan all rebelled against him.
translations.idiomatic: After that his men drifted away, plague and famine struck, and generals Wen Ji and Fu Xuan deserted him.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻陽夏，滅王贊，馳襲蒙城，執晞，署為司馬，月餘乃殺之。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Yangxia, destroyed Wang Zan, galloped to raid Mengcheng, seized Xi, appointed him Marshal, and after more than a month then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le stormed Yangxia, wiped out Wang Zan, raced to Mengcheng, captured Gou Xi, briefly kept him as marshal, then killed him within a month.

sentences.zh: 晞無子，弟純亦遇害。

translations.literal: Xi had no sons; younger brother Chun also met harm.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi left no sons; his brother Gou Chun perished with him.

sentences.zh: 華軼

translations.literal: Hua Die.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Die

sentences.zh: 華軼，字彥夏，平原人，魏太尉歆之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Hua Die, courtesy name Yancai, was a man of Pingyuan, great-grandson of Wei Grand Commandant Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Die, courtesy name Yancai, came from Pingyuan and was the great-grandson of Wei grand commandant Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 祖表，太中大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Biao was Grand Counselor of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hua Biao served as grand counselor of the palace.

sentences.zh: 父澹，河南尹。

translations.literal: His father Dan was Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Hua Dan, had been intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 軼少有才氣，聞於當世，泛愛博納，眾論美之。

translations.literal: Die in youth had talent and spirit, was heard of in the age, broadly loved and broadly accepted, and the crowd’s discussion praised him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Hua Die was talented and celebrated, generous to all, and widely admired.

sentences.zh: 初為博士，累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: At first he was Erudite; by successive promotions he reached Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He began as an erudite and rose to gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 東海王越牧兗州，引為留府長史。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Donghai, Yue, shepherded Yan province, he brought him in as Chief Clerk of the Rear Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue governed Yan province he named Hua Die chief clerk of his rear headquarters.

sentences.zh: 永嘉中，曆振威將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Yongjia period he passed through General Who Rouses Might and Inspector of Jiang province.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongjia he served as General Who Rouses Might and inspector of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 雖逢喪亂，每崇典禮，置儒林祭酒以弘道訓，乃下教曰：「今大義頹替，禮典無宗，朝廷滯議，莫能攸正，常以慨然，宜特立此官，以弘其事。

translations.literal: Although he met mourning and disorder, he always honored canonical rites, set up a Libationer for Confucian Scholars to enlarge the Way’s instruction, then issued instruction, saying: "Now great righteousness has collapsed and replaced, ritual canons have no ancestor, court discussions stagnate and none can rectify them—We constantly have been moved and think it fitting to establish this office alone to enlarge this affair.
translations.idiomatic: Even amid chaos he upheld ritual, created the post of libationer for Confucian scholars, and announced, "Great principle has collapsed and standards are lost; court debate stalls with no one to fix it—I mean to appoint a libationer to revive learning.

sentences.zh: 軍諮祭酒杜夷，棲情玄遠，確然絕俗，才學精博，道行優備，其以為儒林祭酒。

translations.literal: Army Consultant Libationer Du Yi lodges his intent in mystery and distance, is decisively cut off from vulgar ways, talent and learning are precise and broad, conduct of the Way is superior and complete—him We make Libationer for Confucian Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Army consultant Du Yi lives withdrawn in study, stands apart from the vulgar crowd, and unites learning with conduct—let him be libationer for Confucian scholars."

sentences.zh: 」俄被越檄使助討諸賊，軼遣前江夏太守陶侃為揚武將軍，率兵三千屯夏口，以為聲援。

translations.literal: Soon he received Yue’s summons to assist in campaigning against the various bandits; Die sent former Administrator of Jiangxia Tao Kan as General Who Rouses Martiality, leading three thousand troops to encamp at Xiakou as a sound support.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sima Yue ordered him against the rebels; Hua Die sent the former Jiangxia administrator Tao Kan as General Who Rouses Martiality with three thousand men to Xiakou as a demonstration.

sentences.zh: 軼在州其有威惠，州之豪士接以友道，得江表之歡心，流亡之士赴之如歸。

translations.literal: Die in the province had awe-inspiring kindness; the province’s leading knights he received with friend’s way, obtained the heart’s pleasure south of the river, and displaced gentlemen rushed to him as to home.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiang province he balanced severity with mercy, befriended local notables, won the south’s loyalty, and drew refugees as if to a haven.

sentences.zh: 時天子孤危，四方瓦解，軼有匡天下之志，每遣貢獻入洛，不失臣節。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven was orphaned and perilous, the four quarters disintegrated; Die had intent to rectify the empire; each time he sent tribute into Luoyang he did not miss ministerial propriety.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was isolated and the realm splintered, he still meant to restore order and never failed to send tribute east to Luoyang like a loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 謂使者曰：「若洛都道斷，可輸之琅邪王，以明吾之為司馬氏也。

translations.literal: He told the messenger, saying: "If the road to Luoyang is cut off, you may deliver it to the Prince of Langya, to clarify that I act for the house of Sima."
translations.idiomatic: He instructed envoys, "If Luoyang is unreachable, deliver the goods to the Prince of Langya to show that I still serve the house of Sima."

sentences.zh: 」軼自以受洛京所遣，而為壽春所督，時洛京尚存，不能祗承元帝教命，郡縣多諫之，軼不納，曰：「吾欲見詔書耳。

translations.literal: Die himself considered that he was dispatched from Luoyang yet was supervised from Shouchun; at the time Luoyang still existed, and he could not reverently accept the Prince of Langya’s teaching commands; commanderies and counties many remonstrated him, but Die did not accept, saying: "I wish to see edict documents."
translations.idiomatic: He believed his commission came from Luoyang, not from Sima Rui’s headquarters at Shouchun; while the western capital still stood he refused the Prince of Langya’s orders, ignored advice from his magistrates, and said, "I answer only to an imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 」時帝遣揚烈將軍周訪率眾屯彭澤以備軼，訪過姑孰，著作郎干寶見而問之，訪曰：「大府受分，令屯彭澤，彭澤，江州西門也。

translations.literal: At the time the Emperor sent General Who Displays Fierceness Zhou Fang to lead the host to encamp at Pengze to guard against Die; Fang passed Gushu, and Editorial Director Gan Bao saw him and asked him; Fang said: "The great headquarters received division of orders, ordered encampment at Pengze; Pengze is Jiang province’s western gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Zhou Fang, General Who Displays Fierceness, to Pengze to watch Hua Die; passing Gushu he told Gan Bao, "My orders are to hold Pengze—the western gate of Jiang province.

sentences.zh: 華彥夏有憂天下之誠，而不欲碌碌受人控禦，頃來紛紜，粗有嫌隙。

translations.literal: Hua Yancai has sincerity of worrying for the empire, yet does not wish meanly to be controlled and driven; in recent times there has been confusion, roughly some rift and gap.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Die cares for the realm and will not be a puppet; lately we have quarreled and grown apart.

sentences.zh: 今又無故以兵守其門，將成其釁。

translations.literal: Now again without reason using troops to guard his gate, will complete his grievance.
translations.idiomatic: To park troops on his threshold without cause will only deepen the feud.

sentences.zh: 吾當屯尋陽故縣，既在江西，可以捍禦北方，又無嫌於相逼也。

translations.literal: I ought to encamp at the old county of Xunyang; it is already west of the river, can defend the north, and again has no suspicion of pressing each other.
translations.idiomatic: I will instead camp at old Xunyang west of the river—there I can shield the north without seeming to choke him."

sentences.zh: 」尋洛都不守，司空荀籓移檄，而以帝為盟主。

translations.literal: Soon Luoyang did not hold; Minister of Works Xun Fan shifted summons and took the Emperor as covenant lord.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Luoyang fell; minister Xun Fan issued a circular naming Sima Rui covenant chief.

sentences.zh: 既而帝承制改易長吏，軼又不從命，於是遣左將軍王敦都督甘卓、周訪、宋典、趙誘等討之。

translations.literal: Afterward the Emperor by interim authority changed and replaced senior officials; Die again did not follow command; thereupon he sent General of the Left Wang Dun as Area Commander-in-Chief for Gan Zhuo, Zhou Fang, Song Dian, Zhao You, and others to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui began appointing his own governors Hua Die still defied him, so Rui sent Wang Dun to lead Gan Zhuo, Zhou Fang, Song Dian, Zhao You, and others against him.

sentences.zh: 軼遣別駕陳雄屯彭澤以距敦，自為舟軍以為外援。

translations.literal: Die sent Assistant Officer Chen Xiong to encamp at Pengze to resist Dun, himself as boat army to be outer aid.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Die posted Chen Xiong at Pengze to block Wang Dun and kept a river flotilla in reserve.

sentences.zh: 武昌太守馮逸次於湓口，訪擊逸，破之。

translations.literal: Administrator of Wuchang Feng Yi halted at Penkou; Fang attacked Yi and broke him.
translations.idiomatic: Wuchang administrator Feng Yi anchored at Penkou until Zhou Fang smashed him.

sentences.zh: 前江州刺史衛展不為軼所禮，心常怏怏。

translations.literal: Former Inspector of Jiang province Wei Zhan was not treated with ritual by Die; his heart was constantly resentful.
translations.idiomatic: The former Jiang inspector Wei Zhan had been slighted by Hua Die and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 至是，與豫章太守周廣為內應，潛軍襲軼，軼眾潰，奔于安城，追斬之，及其五子，傳首建鄴。

translations.literal: At this point, together with Administrator of Yuzhang Zhou Guang as inner response, he secretly sent troops to raid Die; Die’s host collapsed, fled to Ancheng, was pursued and beheaded, together with his five sons; heads were sent to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: He now joined Yuzhang administrator Zhou Guang in a coup, struck Hua Die’s camp by surprise, hunted him to Ancheng, executed him and his five sons, and sent their heads to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 初，廣陵高悝寓居江州，軼避為西曹掾，尋而軼敗，悝藏匿軼二子及妻，崎嶇經年。

translations.literal: Earlier, Gao Kui of Guangling had lodged in Jiang province; Die had avoided appointing him Western Bureau Attendant; soon Die was defeated, and Kui hid Die’s two sons and wife, ruggedly for a full year.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Kui of Guangling had lived in Jiangzhou; Hua Die had refused him office, yet when Die fell Gao Kui hid Die’s two sons and wife for a year on the run.

sentences.zh: 既而遇赦，悝攜之出首，帝嘉而宥之。

translations.literal: Afterward encountering amnesty, Kui led them out to surrender; the Emperor praised and pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: When an amnesty came he brought them in; the emperor praised and spared him.

sentences.zh: 劉喬

translations.literal: Liu Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao

sentences.zh: 劉喬，字仲彥，南陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Qiao, courtesy name Zhongyan, was a man of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao, courtesy name Zhongyan, came from Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 其先漢宗室，封安眾侯，傳襲曆三代。

translations.literal: His ancestors were Han imperial lineage, enfeoffed Marquis of Anzhong, transmitted and inherited through three generations.
translations.idiomatic: His clan descended from Han imperial stock enfeoffed as marquis of Anzhong for three generations.

sentences.zh: 祖暠，魏侍中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gao was Wei Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Liu Gao had been Wei palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 父阜，陳留相。

translations.literal: His father Fu was Administrator of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: His father, Liu Fu, had governed Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 喬少為秘書郎，建威將軍王戎引為參軍。

translations.literal: Qiao in youth was Secretary Gentleman; General Who Establishes Might Wang Rong brought him in as Army Advisor.
translations.idiomatic: He began as secretary gentleman and joined Wang Rong’s staff as army adviser.

sentences.zh: 伐吳之役，戎使喬與參軍羅尚濟江，破武昌，還授滎陽令，遷太子洗馬。

translations.literal: In the campaign against Wu, Rong sent Qiao together with Army Advisor Luo Shang to cross the river, broke Wuchang, on return was appointed Magistrate of Xingyang, transferred to Household Groom for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the conquest of Wu he crossed the Yangzi with Luo Shang, took Wuchang, then became magistrate of Xingyang and household groom to the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 以誅楊駿功，賜爵關中侯，拜尚書右丞。

translations.literal: By merit in executing Yang Jun he was granted noble rank as Marquis Within the Passes and appointed Right Assistant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: For helping execute Yang Jun he was enfeoffed marquis within the passes and named right assistant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 豫誅賈謐，封安眾男，累遷散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He participated in executing Jia Mi, was enfeoffed as Baron of Anzhong, and by successive promotions reached Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in killing Jia Mi, was made baron of Anzhong, and rose to gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 齊王冏為大司馬，初，嵇紹為冏所重，每下階迎之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qi, Jiong, was Grand Marshal, earlier Ji Shao was valued by Jiong, who each time descended the stairs to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Jiong was grand marshal he honored Ji Shao so deeply that he would descend his steps to greet him.

sentences.zh: 喬言於冏曰；

translations.literal: Qiao spoke to Jiong, saying;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao told Sima Jiong,

sentences.zh: 「裴、張之誅，朝臣畏憚孫秀，故不敢不受財物。

translations.literal: "At the executions of Pei and Zhang, court ministers feared Sun Xiu and therefore did not dare refuse to accept goods.
translations.idiomatic: "After Pei and Zhang were killed the ministers feared Sun Xiu and dared not refuse his bribes.

sentences.zh: 嵇紹今何所逼忌，故畜裴家車牛、張家奴婢邪？

translations.literal: What compulsion or taboo does Ji Shao have now, that he therefore stores Pei family carts and oxen and Zhang family slave girls?
translations.idiomatic: What hold does anyone have on Ji Shao that he should warehouse Pei’s carts and oxen and Zhang’s bondmaids?

sentences.zh: 樂彥輔來，公未嘗下床，何獨加敬於紹？

translations.literal: When Le Yanfu came, the duke never once descended the bed—why alone add respect to Shao?
translations.idiomatic: You never left your couch for Le Yanfu—why single out Ji Shao for such honors?

sentences.zh: 」冏乃止。

translations.literal: " Jiong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Jiong dropped the practice.

sentences.zh: 紹謂喬曰：「大司馬何故不復迎客？

translations.literal: Shao said to Qiao: "Why does the Grand Marshal no longer receive guests?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao asked Liu Qiao why the grand marshal had stopped receiving visitors.

translations.literal: Closing quotation mark and period (scribe’s fragment closing Ji Shao’s speech).
translations.idiomatic: (End of Ji Shao’s question.)

sentences.zh: 喬曰：「似有正人言，以卿不足迎者。

translations.literal: Qiao said: "It seems a upright man spoke, considering you not worth welcoming.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao answered, "Some honest man must have said Ji Shao was not worth the courtesy."

sentences.zh: 」紹曰：「正人為誰？

translations.literal: " Shao said: "Who was the upright man?
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao asked, "Who was this paragon of virtue?

sentences.zh: 」喬曰：「其則不遠。

translations.literal: " Qiao said: "That rule is not far to seek.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao answered, "You will find him close at hand."

sentences.zh: 」紹默然。

translations.literal: " Shao was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Shao had no reply.

sentences.zh: 頃之，遷御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Palace Assistant Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was promoted to Palace Assistant Secretary.

sentences.zh: 冏腹心董艾勢傾朝廷，百僚莫敢忤旨。

translations.literal: Jiong’s intimate Dong Ai’s power tilted the court; of the hundred officials none dared disobey intent.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ai, Sima Jiong’s favorite, dominated the court, and no minister dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 喬二旬之中，奏劾艾罪釁者六。

translations.literal: Within two ten-day periods Qiao memorialized impeaching Ai’s crimes and faults six times.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty days Liu Qiao filed six memorials detailing Dong Ai’s crimes.

sentences.zh: 艾諷尚書右丞苟晞免喬官，復為屯騎校尉。

translations.literal: Ai hinted to Right Assistant in the Masters of Writing Gou Xi to dismiss Qiao from office; he again became Colonel of Garrison Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ai persuaded Gou Xi, right assistant in the Masters of Writing, to strip Liu Qiao of his post; Qiao was relegated to colonel of garrison cavalry.

sentences.zh: 張昌之亂，喬出為威遠將軍、豫州刺史，與荊州刺史劉弘共討昌，進左將軍。

translations.literal: In Zhang Chang’s rebellion Qiao went out as General Who Deters from Afar and Inspector of Yu province, together with Jing province Inspector Liu Hong jointly campaigned against Chang, and was advanced General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rose, Liu Qiao became General Who Deters from Afar and inspector of Yu province, joined Liu Hong of Jing in the suppression, and was promoted to General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 惠帝西幸長安，喬與諸州郡舉兵迎大駕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui went west to Chang’an, Qiao together with the various provinces and commanderies raised troops to welcome the Grand Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui withdrew to Chang’an, Liu Qiao and other provinces mobilized to escort the throne back east.

sentences.zh: 東海王越承制轉喬安北將軍、冀州刺史，以范陽王虓領豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, by interim authority transferred Qiao to General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Ji province, and had the Prince of Fanyang, Xiao, hold Inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince of Donghai, reassigned Liu Qiao as General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Ji province while naming Sima Xiao, Prince of Fanyang, acting inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 喬以虓非天子命，不受代，發兵距之。

translations.literal: Qiao because Xiao was not the Son of Heaven’s order, did not accept replacement, and raised troops to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao refused to yield because Sima Xiao lacked an imperial mandate, and took up arms to resist him.

sentences.zh: 潁川太守劉輿昵于虓，喬上尚書列輿罪惡。

translations.literal: Yingchuan Administrator Liu Yu was intimate with Xiao; Qiao sent up to the Masters of Writing listing Yu’s crimes and evils.
translations.idiomatic: Yingchuan’s Liu Yu was Sima Xiao’s confidant, so Liu Qiao memorialized the capital with a bill of particulars against him.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒得喬所上，乃宣詔使鎮南將軍劉弘、征東大將軍劉准、平南將軍彭城王釋與喬並力攻虓於許昌。

translations.literal: The Prince of Hejian, Yong, obtaining what Qiao had sent up, then proclaimed an edict ordering General Who Guards the South Liu Hong, General Who Conquers the East Liu Zhun, General Who Pacifies the South Prince Shi of Pengcheng, and Qiao jointly to attack Xiao at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, took Liu Qiao’s memorials and issued orders for Liu Hong, Liu Zhun, Prince Shi of Pengcheng, and Liu Qiao to converge on Sima Xiao at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 輿弟琨率眾救虓，未至而虓敗，虓乃與琨俱奔河北。

translations.literal: Yu’s younger brother Kun led the host to rescue Xiao; before he arrived Xiao was defeated, and Xiao then together with Kun both fled to north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun marched to relieve Sima Xiao, but Xiao collapsed before he arrived; Xiao fled north of the Yellow River with Liu Kun.

sentences.zh: 未幾，琨率突騎五千濟河攻喬，喬劫琨父蕃，以檻車載之，據考城以距虓，眾不敵而潰。

translations.literal: Before long Kun led five thousand raiding cavalry crossed the river to attack Qiao; Qiao seized Kun’s father Fan, carried him in a cage cart, occupied Kaocheng to resist Xiao, the host not matching and collapsing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Kun forded the Yellow River with five thousand horse; Liu Qiao seized Liu Kun’s father Liu Fan, caged him, and held Kaocheng until his lines broke under pressure.

sentences.zh: 喬復收散卒，屯于平氏，河間王顒進喬鎮東將軍、假節，以其長子祐為東郡太守，又遣劉弘、劉准、彭城王釋等率兵援喬。

translations.literal: Qiao again gathered scattered troops and encamped at Pingshi; the Prince of Hejian, Yong, advanced Qiao to General Who Guards the East with credential staff, made his eldest son You Administrator of Dong commandery, and again sent Liu Hong, Liu Zhun, Prince Shi of Pengcheng, and others to lead troops to aid Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao rallied at Pingshi; Sima Yong promoted him to General Who Guards the East with staff, named his son Liu You administrator of Dong commandery, and sent Liu Hong, Liu Zhun, and Prince Shi to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 弘與喬箋曰：「適承范陽欲代明使君。

translations.literal: Hong wrote a note to Qiao, saying: "I have just learned the Prince of Fanyang wishes to replace the enlightened envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong wrote to Liu Qiao: "I hear Sima Xiao intends to replace you.

sentences.zh: 明使君受命本朝，列居方伯，當官而行，同獎王室，橫見遷代，誠為不允。

translations.literal: The enlightened envoy received mandate from this court, ranks among regional shepherds, ought to act for office and together aid the royal house; to be capriciously moved and replaced is truly not fitting.
translations.idiomatic: You hold an imperial commission as a regional commander and should serve the throne; an arbitrary replacement is unjust.

sentences.zh: 然古人有言，牽牛以蹊人之田，信有罪矣，而奪之牛，罰亦重矣。

translations.literal: Yet the ancients had a saying: leading an ox to tread another’s field is indeed guilt, yet to seize his ox—the punishment is also heavy.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: driving your ox across another’s furrow is wrong, but confiscating the ox is excessive punishment.

sentences.zh: 明使君不忍亮直狷介之忿，甘為戎首，竊以為過。

translations.literal: If the enlightened envoy cannot bear straightforward and narrow resentment, willingly becomes spearhead of arms, We privately think it a fault.
translations.idiomatic: If you nurse a private grudge and become the first to draw swords, I think that a mistake.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 至人之道，用行舍藏。

translations.literal: The way of the perfected person is to use when it goes, store when it hides.
translations.idiomatic: The sage acts when the time serves and withdraws when it does not.

sentences.zh: 跨下之辱，猶宜俯就，況於換代之嫌，纖介之釁哉！

translations.literal: The humiliation under a bridge is still fitting to bow to—how much more for the suspicion of replacement, a hair’s-breadth rift!
translations.idiomatic: Even the humiliation under a bridge must be borne when necessary—let alone a quarrel over a post!

sentences.zh: 范陽國屬，使君庶姓，周之宗盟，疏不間親，曲直既均，責有所在。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fanyang is a state cadet branch, the envoy is a lesser surname; in Zhou’s clan covenants the distant does not come between the close—once right and wrong are balanced, responsibility has its place.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao is a cadet prince and you are another surname; in the Zhou model kinship outweighs distance—once justice is weighed, blame falls where it belongs.

sentences.zh: 廉藺區區戰國之將，猶能升降以利社稷，況命世之士哉！

translations.literal: Lian and Lin, mere generals of the Warring States, still could rise and fall for the altars’ sake—how much more a man who commands his age!
translations.idiomatic: Even Lian Po and Lin Xiangru, mere Warring States generals, swallowed pride for the state—how much more should you?

sentences.zh: 今天下紛紜，主上播越，正是忠臣義士同心戮力之時。

translations.literal: Now the empire is in turmoil, the lord is cast about—this is precisely the hour when loyal ministers and righteous knights join hearts and join strength.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is in chaos and the emperor adrift—this is when loyal men must pull together.

sentences.zh: 弘實暗劣，過蒙國恩，願與使君共戴盟主，雁行下風，掃除凶寇，救蒼生之倒懸，反北辰於太極。

translations.literal: Hong is truly dim and weak, excessively burdened with state grace; I wish with the envoy together to bear the covenant lord, goose-line in the lower wind, sweep away the fierce bandits, rescue the black-haired people’s inverted hanging, return the north pivot to the supreme pole.
translations.idiomatic: I am a mediocre man overfavored by the court, yet I beg you to join me under the covenant chief, fall in behind him like geese in flight, drive off the rebels, lift the people from their peril, and set the throne aright.

sentences.zh: 此功未立，不宜乖離。

translations.literal: This merit not yet established, it is not fitting to split apart.
translations.idiomatic: Until that work is done we should not divide our forces.

sentences.zh: 備蒙顧遇，情隆于常，披露丹誠，不敢不盡。

translations.literal: Having fully received your regard, my feeling rises beyond the ordinary; laying bare cinnabar sincerity, I dare not exhaust all.
translations.idiomatic: You have honored me beyond the usual; I lay my heart bare and speak without reserve.

sentences.zh: 春秋之時，諸侯相伐，復為和親者多矣。

translations.literal: In Spring and Autumn times the feudal lords attacked one another, yet those who afterward made peace and kinship were many.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the Spring and Autumn era rivals often made peace after war.

sentences.zh: 願明使君回既往之恨，追不二之蹤，解連環之結，修如初之好。

translations.literal: I wish the enlightened envoy to turn back past hatred, pursue tracks of no second thought, undo knotted chains, and restore friendship as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Turn from old anger, seek reconciliation, untie this knot, and renew your former amity.

sentences.zh: 范陽亦將悔前之失，思崇後信矣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fanyang too will repent prior faults and think to honor later good faith.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao will regret his rashness and honor a fresh pledge.

sentences.zh: 東海王越將討喬，弘又與越書曰：「適聞以吾州將擅舉兵逐范陽，當討之，誠明同異、懲禍亂之宜。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, will campaign against Qiao; Hong again wrote to Yue, saying: "I have just heard that because my province’s general rashly raised troops to expel the Prince of Fanyang, you will punish him—truly it is the right way to clarify right and wrong and chastise rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yue prepared to strike Liu Qiao, Liu Hong wrote again: "I hear you mean to punish our general for driving out Sima Xiao—a proper response to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 然吾竊謂不可。

translations.literal: Yet We privately say it cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: Yet I believe you should not."

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: "Why?

sentences.zh: 今北辰遷居，元首移幸，群後抗義以謀王室，吾州將荷國重恩，列位方伯，亦伐鼓即戎，戮力致命之秋也。

translations.literal: Now the north pivot has moved residence, the chief head has shifted fortune; the throng of lords resist in righteousness to plan the royal house; my province’s general bears the state’s heavy grace, ranks among regional shepherds, and this too is the autumn of beating drums and taking arms, joining strength to exhaust life.
translations.idiomatic: The capital has moved and the emperor is on the road; lords everywhere rise for the dynasty. Our general holds a weighty commission—this is the season to beat the drum and spend every life in the king’s service.

sentences.zh: 而范陽代之，吾州將不從，由代之不允，但矯枉過正，更以為罪耳。

translations.literal: Yet the Prince of Fanyang replaced him; my province’s general did not follow—because the replacement was not fitting, only straightening the crooked passed the mark, and again was made crime.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiao tried to replace him unjustly; our general refused because the order was wrong—only zeal overshot the mark, not treason.

sentences.zh: 昔齊桓赦射鉤之仇而相管仲，晉文忘斬祛之怨而親勃鞮，方之於今，當何有哉！

translations.literal: In antiquity Duke Huan of Qi pardoned the arrow-on-the-bowstring grudge and made Guan Zhong minister; Duke Wen of Jin forgot the cut-sleeve resentment and drew near Bo Di—compared to today, what should there be!
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan forgave Guan Zhong’s murder attempt; Duke Wen embraced Bo Di after trying to kill him—how petty is today’s quarrel by comparison!

sentences.zh: 且君子躬自厚而薄責於人，今奸臣弄權，朝廷困逼，此四海之所危懼，宜釋私嫌，共存公義，含垢匿瑕，忍所難忍，以大逆為先，奉迎為急，不可思小怨忘大德也。

translations.literal: Moreover the gentleman is strict on himself and light in blaming others; now wicked ministers manipulate power, the court is pressed in difficulty—this is what the four seas fears; it is fitting to release private grudges, together preserve public righteousness, bear filth and hide flaws, endure what is hard to endure, take the great rebellion as first, welcoming the sovereign as urgent—not to ponder small resentments and forget great virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman is hardest on himself; with villains twisting the court the whole realm trembles—set private scores aside, uphold the public good, swallow insults, treat the great rebels as the first foe and the emperor’s return as the urgent task, and do not sacrifice the greater duty to pique.

sentences.zh: 苟崇忠恕，共明分局，連旗推鋒，各致臣節，吾州將必輸寫肝膽，以報所蒙，實不足計一朝之謬，發赫然之怒，使韓盧東郭相困而為豺狼之擒也。

translations.literal: If you truly honor loyalty and forgiveness, together clarify divided offices, join banners and push spears, each exhaust ministerial propriety, my province’s general will surely pour out liver and gall to repay what he has received—it is really not worth reckoning one morning’s slip and unleashing terrible wrath, letting Han’s hounds and Dongguo mutually trap each other and be seized by jackals and wolves.
translations.idiomatic: If you show good faith and clear lines of command, our general will give you his utmost; do not for one morning’s mistake loose a rage that leaves both sides tangled like the hounds of Han and the rabbit of Dongguo for jackals to devour.

sentences.zh: 吾雖庶姓，負乘過分，實願足下率齊內外，以康王室，竊恥同儕自為蠹害。

translations.literal: Although We are a lesser surname, bearing the carriage beyond allotment; We truly wish you, sir, to align within and without to bring peace to the royal house; We privately are shamed that peers wound one another like worms in the wood.
translations.idiomatic: I am no kinsman of yours and hold office beyond my deserts, yet I beg you to steady the house of Sima within and without; I am ashamed to see allies tear at one another like borers in timber.

sentences.zh: 貪獻所懷，惟足下圖之。

translations.literal: Greedy to present what We hold in the breast—only you, sir, chart it.
translations.idiomatic: I offer these thoughts in all bluntness—please weigh them."

sentences.zh: 」又上表曰：「范陽王虓欲代豫州刺史喬，喬舉兵逐虓，司空、東海王越以喬不從命討之。

translations.literal: " Again he submitted a memorial, saying: "The Prince of Fanyang, Xiao, wished to replace Inspector of Yu province Qiao; Qiao raised troops to expel Xiao; the Minister of Works, the Prince of Donghai, Yue, because Qiao did not follow command campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "Sima Xiao sought to replace Liu Qiao as inspector of Yu; Liu Qiao drove him out; Sima Yue attacked Qiao for disobedience.

sentences.zh: 臣以為喬忝受殊恩，顯居州司，自欲立功于時，以徇國難，無他罪闕，而范陽代之，代之為非。

translations.literal: Your subject considers that Qiao has disgraced receiving special grace, prominently occupies provincial office, himself wished to establish merit in the time to follow the state’s difficulty—he has no other fault or lack, while the Prince of Fanyang replacing him—the replacement was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao owed the throne much and held a great post; he meant only to serve in crisis and committed no other crime, whereas Sima Xiao’s replacement was illegitimate.

sentences.zh: 然喬亦不得以虓之非，專威輒討，誠應顯戮以懲不恪。

translations.literal: Yet Qiao also could not because of Xiao’s wrong alone seize authority and campaign—truly he ought to be openly executed to punish lack of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Liu Qiao was wrong to wage private war; he deserved public censure.

sentences.zh: 然自頃兵戈紛亂，猜禍鋒生，恐疑隙構于群王，災難延于宗子，權柄隆於朝廷，逆順效於成敗，今夕為忠，明旦為逆，翩其反而，互為戎首，載籍以來，骨肉之禍未有如今者也。

translations.literal: Yet from of late arms and spears have been tangled in chaos, suspicion and disaster’s point have sprung up; We fear rifts will be built among the throng of princes, disasters extend to the imperial sons, power handles swell at court, obedience and rebellion follow success and failure—tonight loyal, tomorrow treacherous, fluttering their reversal, each becoming spearhead of arms; since records began, kin-flesh calamities have never been like the present.
translations.idiomatic: Still, war breeds suspicion among princes, disaster among imperial kin, and shifting loyalties at court—never have royal houses suffered such mutual slaughter.

sentences.zh: 臣竊悲之，痛心疾首。

translations.literal: Your subject privately grieves for it, pains heart and splits head.
translations.idiomatic: I grieve to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 今邊陲無備豫之儲，中華有杼軸之困，而股肱之臣不惟國體，職競尋常，自相楚剝，為害轉深，積毀銷骨。

translations.literal: Now the frontier has no stores of precaution; the central Hua has shuttle-and-loom distress; yet the thigh-and-arm ministers do not think of the state’s body, zealously compete in the ordinary, mutually Chu-peel one another, harm grows deeper, piled slander melts bone.
translations.idiomatic: The borders are bare, the heartland exhausted, yet ministers claw at one another like worms in the guts of the state until slander wears bone away.

sentences.zh: 萬一四夷乘虛為變，此亦猛獸交鬪，自效于卞莊者矣。

translations.literal: Should the four barbarians by emptiness make change, this too is fierce beasts crossing bite, offering themselves to Bian Zhuang’s prey.
translations.idiomatic: If the barbarians strike while we feud, we are only tigers tearing each other for Bian Zhuang’s kill.

sentences.zh: 臣以為宜速發明詔，詔越等令兩釋猜嫌，各保分局。

translations.literal: Your subject considers it fitting speedily to issue a clear edict, ordering Yue and others to order both sides to release mutual suspicion, each guarding divided offices.
translations.idiomatic: I urge a clear edict commanding Sima Yue and both camps to drop their suspicions and hold their assigned posts.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，其有不被詔書擅興兵馬者，天下共伐之。

translations.literal: From this onward, whoever does not receive edict documents yet rashly raises troops and horses—the empire together shall punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth any who mobilize without an edict may be attacked by all.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云：『誰能執熱，逝不以濯？

translations.literal: The Odes says: "Who can take hold of what is hot and will not go to bathe?
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Poetry says, "Who can grasp what burns and not plunge into water?

sentences.zh: 』若誠濯之，必無灼爛之患，永有泰山之固矣。」

translations.literal: " If indeed you bathe in it, there will surely be no scorching disaster, eternally having Mount Tai’s solidity."
translations.idiomatic: Cool the grudge and you avoid the burn; you will stand firm as Mount Tai."

sentences.zh: 時河間王顒方距關東，倚喬為助，不納其言。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Hejian, Yong, was just resisting the east of the pass, leaned on Qiao as aid, and did not accept his words.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong, still holding the pass against the east, needed Liu Qiao and ignored this advice.

sentences.zh: 東海王越移檄天下，帥甲士三萬，將入關迎大駕，軍次於蕭，喬懼，遣子祐距越于蕭縣之靈壁。

translations.literal: The Prince of Donghai, Yue, shifted summons to the empire, led armored soldiers thirty thousand, about to enter the pass to welcome the Grand Carriage; the army halted at Xiao; Qiao feared and sent son You to resist Yue at Lingbi in Xiao county.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue summoned the realm, marched thirty thousand men toward the pass to recover the emperor, and halted at Xiao; Liu Qiao sent Liu You to block him at Lingbi.

sentences.zh: 劉琨分兵向許昌，許昌人納之。

translations.literal: Liu Kun divided troops toward Xuchang; the people of Xuchang admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun detached a column toward Xuchang, and the city opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 琨自滎陽率兵迎越，遇祐，眾潰見殺。

translations.literal: Kun from Xingyang led troops to welcome Yue, encountered You, the host collapsed and he was seen killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun marched from Xingyang to join Sima Yue, met Liu You, was routed, and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 喬眾遂散，與五百騎奔平氏。

translations.literal: Qiao’s host thereupon scattered; with five hundred cavalry he fled to Pingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao’s army melted away; he fled to Pingshi with five hundred horse.

sentences.zh: 帝還洛陽，大赦，越復表喬為太傅軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: The Emperor returned to Luoyang, great amnesty; Yue again memorialized Qiao as Libationer for Army Consultation to the Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned to Luoyang under general amnesty, Sima Yue again named Liu Qiao libationer for army consultation to the grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 越薨，復以喬為都督豫州諸軍事、鎮東將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: When Yue died, again Qiao was made Area Commander-in-Chief for military affairs of Yu province, General Who Guards the East, and Inspector of Yu province.
translations.idiomatic: After Sima Yue died Liu Qiao was restored as military governor of Yu, General Who Guards the East, and inspector of Yu.

sentences.zh: 卒于官，時年六十三。

translations.literal: He died in office at age sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office at sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 湣帝末，追贈司空。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Min’s reign he was posthumously awarded Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Min he was posthumously named minister of works.

sentences.zh: 子挺，潁川太守。

translations.literal: His son Ting was Administrator of Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Ting became administrator of Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 挺子耽。

translations.literal: Ting’s son Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ting’s son Dan

sentences.zh: 孫耽

translations.literal: Sun Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan; the transmitted text writes the surname as Sun.

sentences.zh: =耽字敬道。

translations.literal: =Dan, courtesy name Jingdao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dan, courtesy name Jingdao,

sentences.zh: 少有行檢，以義尚流稱，為宗族所推。

translations.literal: In youth he had conduct and restraint, by righteousness was praised in current talk, and was pushed by the lineage group.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was disciplined and esteemed for integrity, and his clan looked to him.

sentences.zh: 博學，明習《詩》、《禮》、三史。

translations.literal: He was broadly learned, clearly practiced the Odes, the Rites, and the Three Histories.
translations.idiomatic: He was widely read in the Odes, the Rites, and the three histories.

sentences.zh: 曆度支尚書，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He passed through Masters of Writing for Revenue, added Gentleman of the Household for All Purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He served as masters of writing for revenue and gentleman for all purposes.

sentences.zh: 在職公平廉慎，所蒞著績。

translations.literal: In office he was fair, impartial, honest, and careful; wherever he presided he showed merit.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was fair, frugal, and left a record of achievement.

sentences.zh: 桓玄，耽女婿也。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan was Dan’s son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan was his son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 及玄輔政，以耽為尚書令，加侍中，不拜，改授特進、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Xuan assisted the government, he made Dan Masters of Writing chief with added Palace Attendant; he did not accept appointment, was changed to grant Exceptional Advance, Grand Master of Golden Purple Gleam.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan took power he offered Dan the chief ministership with palace attendant rank; Dan declined and accepted exceptional advance and grand master of golden purple gleam instead.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，追贈左光祿大夫、開府。

translations.literal: Soon he died, posthumously awarded Grand Master of the Left Gleam, opening office.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously named grand master of the left gleam with independent headquarters.

sentences.zh: 耽子柳。

translations.literal: Dan’s son Liu (heading).
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Liu (section heading).

sentences.zh: 耽子柳

translations.literal: Dan’s son Liu (repeated heading in source).
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Liu (repeated heading).

sentences.zh: =柳字叔惠，亦有名譽。

translations.literal: =Liu, courtesy name Shuhui, also had reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu, courtesy name Shuhui, also enjoyed a fine name.

sentences.zh: 少登清官，曆尚書左右僕射。

translations.literal: In youth he ascended pure offices, passed through Left and Right Vice Directors of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through pure posts to vice director of the Masters of Writing on both left and right.

sentences.zh: 時右丞傅迪好廣讀書而不解其義，柳唯讀《老子》而已，迪每輕之。

translations.literal: At the time Right Assistant Fu Di loved broadly to read books yet did not understand their meaning; Liu alone read only the Laozi; Di constantly belittled him.
translations.idiomatic: The right assistant Fu Di read widely but shallowly; Liu Liu studied only the Laozi, and Fu mocked him.

sentences.zh: 柳云：「卿讀書雖多，而無所解，可謂書簏矣。

translations.literal: Liu said: "Sir, although you read many books, you understand none—it may be called a book basket.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liu retorted, "You read librariesful and understand nothing—you are a walking bookcase.

sentences.zh: 」時人重其言。

translations.literal: " People of the time valued his words.
translations.idiomatic: The age respected the barb.

sentences.zh: 出為徐、兗、江三州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Xu, Yan, and Jiang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He became inspector of Xu, Yan, and Jiang provinces in turn.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: At death he was awarded Grand Master of the Right Gleam, opening office with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At his death the court named him grand master of the right gleam with three excellencies–rank ceremony.

sentences.zh: 喬弟乂，始安太守。

translations.literal: Qiao’s younger brother Yi was Administrator of Shi’an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao’s brother Liu Yi governed Shi’an.

sentences.zh: 乂子成，丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Yi’s son Cheng was Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi’s son Liu Cheng became intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 史評

translations.literal: Historians’ judgment.
translations.idiomatic: The historians’ verdict

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：周浚人倫鑒悟，周馥理識精詳，華軼動顧禮經，劉喬志存諒直，用能曆官內外，咸著勳庸。

translations.literal: The court historians say: Zhou Jun in judging men was perceptive; Zhou Fu’s principles and insight were precise and detailed; Hua Die moved in accord with ritual canons; Liu Qiao’s intent lay in straightforward integrity—thereby they could pass through office within and without and all show merit and service.
translations.idiomatic: The historians say: Zhou Jun read character keenly; Zhou Fu’s judgment was exact; Hua Die heeded the rites; Liu Qiao stood for plain integrity—each served inside and outside court with real achievement.

sentences.zh: 而祖宣獻策遷都，乖忤於東海，彥夏系心宸極，獲罪於琅邪，乃被以惡名，加其顯戮，豈不哀哉！

translations.literal: Yet Zuxuan presented a plan to move the capital and went against the Prince of Donghai; Yancai tied his heart to the polar throne and earned guilt from the Prince of Langya—thereupon they were covered with evil names and subjected to manifest execution—is it not pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhou Fu’s capital plan crossed Sima Yue; Hua Die’s loyalty to Luoyang angered Sima Rui—both were slandered and struck down, a bitter fate.

sentences.zh: 向若違左衤任于伊川，建右社於淮服，據方城之險，藉全楚之資，簡練吳越之兵，漕引淮海之粟，縱未能祈天永命，猶足以紓難緩亡。

translations.literal: Had they turned from the left barbarian collar at the Yi River, built the right soil-altar on the Huai domain, held the Fang citadel’s peril, relied on all Chu’s resources, drilled Wu and Yue’s troops, and canal-fed Huai and Hai grain—even if they could not pray Heaven for endless mandate, still it would have sufficed to loosen difficulty and slow ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Had they fortified the central plains, built new altars on the Huai, held Xiangyang’s heights, mobilized Chu’s strength, trained southern troops, and fed armies from the Huai canals, they might not have won eternity, but they could have bought time against ruin.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 「不用其良，覆俾我悖」，其此之謂也。

translations.literal: "Not using their good men, overturning makes us reckless"—it is this of which it speaks.
translations.idiomatic: As the Classic of Poetry says, "They would not use their good officers, and brought themselves to this confusion"—just so here.

sentences.zh: 苟晞擢自庸微，位居上將，釋位之功未立，貪暴之釁已彰，假手世龍，以至屠戮，斯所謂「殺人多矣，能無及此乎」！

translations.literal: Gou Xi was raised from mean and slight, reached position of highest general; merit of releasing office not yet established, the stink of greed and cruelty was already manifest; borrowing the hand of Shilong, thereby reaching slaughter and execution—this is what is called "having killed many—can one not reach this point!"
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi rose from obscurity to supreme command without earning grace by yielding power; his greed and cruelty were notorious, and Shi Le—styled Shilong—finished him. So runs the adage: "He who slays too many cannot escape the reckoning."

sentences.zh: 贊曰：開林才理，爰登貴仕，績著折沖，化行江汜。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: Kailin by talent and principle, then ascended noble office; merit showed in Subduing the Foe, transformation went along the Jiang’s banks.
translations.idiomatic: The verdict reads: Zhou Jun by talent rose high, broke enemies on the Yangzi, and spread order along the river.

sentences.zh: 軼既尊主，馥亦勤王，背時獲戾，違天不祥。

translations.literal: Die already honored the lord; Fu also toiled for the king; turning from the times they got blame; opposing Heaven is inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Die honored the emperor; Zhou Fu labored for him; both were out of step with the hour and paid for it.

sentences.zh: 喬為戎首，未識行藏。

translations.literal: Qiao became spearhead of arms, not knowing to go or hide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao drew first sword without knowing when to yield.

sentences.zh: 道將鞠旅，威名克舉，領虐有聞，忠勤未取。

translations.literal: Daojiang reviewed hosts, awe-inspiring name could be raised; greedy cruelty was heard of, loyalty and diligence were not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Daojiang drilled armies and won renown, yet cruelty was his legend and loyal service went unrewarded.
